posts.title: 2026 tourist taxes by city: what you actually pay per night
posts.summary: A city-by-city table of 2026 tourist taxes, visitor levies and overnight fees, compiled from the same official-source research as our destination pages. No invented rates.
posts.body:
Hotel rates are not the bill. In 2026 a growing list of cities add a tourist tax, visitor levy, green tax or climate fee on top of the room, and several of those rates moved this year. The numbers below are the ones we already published, destination by destination, after checking operator and government sources at the time of writing. Where a figure is a percentage of the room rate, do the maths on the net rate, not the package price you saw on a booking site.

This is not a complete world list. It is every destination on RuinMyTrip where we could pin down a current overnight tax. Day-tripper access fees (Venice) and airport departure fees (Maldives) are called out separately because they are not the same thing as a hotel tax, even though they hit the same trip budget.

Overnight tourist taxes in 2026

City2026 rateHow it is charged
Amsterdam12.5% of net room price, the highest in Europe, plus 21% Dutch VAT on accommodation from 1 January 2026Per night, on the room. The coalition plans a rise from 12.5% to 16% in 2027. Stacked, tax is roughly a third of the quoted room rate.
Barcelona4.50 EUR Catalan regional rate plus 5 EUR city surcharge per person per night, plus 10% VAT, from 1 April 2026About 12 EUR per person per night at five-star hotels (up from 7.50 EUR in 2025), 8.40 EUR at four-star, 9.50 EUR on short-term rentals. The city surcharge rises 1 EUR a year through 2029.
Berlin7.5% of the net accommodation price (Ubernachtungsteuer), unchanged since 1 January 2025Applies to business stays as well as leisure, since 1 April 2024. Operators file quarterly via ELSTER.
Edinburgh5% visitor levy on paid overnight accommodation, first 5 consecutive nightsTook effect 24 July 2026. Applies to bookings made on or after 1 October 2025. Projected to raise up to 50 million pounds a year.
Hong Kong3% hotel accommodation taxReintroduced in 2025, still in effect in 2026.
KyotoFive-tier lodging tax from March 2026: 200 yen (under 6,000), 400 yen (6,000-19,999), 1,000 yen (20,000-49,999), 4,000 yen (50,000-99,999), 10,000 yen (100,000+)Per person per night, based on the room rate band.
Lisbon4 EUR per person per nightGuests aged 13 and over, capped at 7 nights. Raised from 2 EUR on 1 September 2024.
MaldivesResort green tax 12 USD per person per night (doubled from 6 USD on 1 January 2025). Smaller properties collect 6 USD.Earmarked for reef protection. On top of that, airport departure fees for foreigners rose to 50 USD economy, 120 USD business, 240 USD first class.
Milan10 EUR per person per night at 4-star hotels; 9.50 EUR for vacation rentals and tourist apartmentsEffective 1 April 2026, Municipal Council resolution no. 144 of 12 February 2026.
NiceRoughly 1.50 to 6.00 EUR per person per nightUnclassified properties (most short-term rentals) are charged 1 to 5% of the per-person nightly rate excluding VAT, capped at the highest local rate.
Osaka200 yen (5,000 to under 15,000 yen rooms), 400 yen (15,000 to under 20,000), 500 yen (20,000+). Rooms under 5,000 yen are exempt.Per person per night since 1 September 2025. From 1 March 2026 it is charged separately from the room rate and paid on-site even for prepaid bookings.
Porto3 EUR per person per night, up from about 2 EURCapped at 7 nights, 21 EUR maximum per trip.
PragueCZK 50 per person per nightPrague 1 has proposed about CZK 175 (roughly 7 EUR). That is a proposal, not the current rate.
Reykjavik800 ISK per lodging unit per night for hotels and guesthouses; 400 ISK for campsites and motorhome pitchesIceland lodging tax effective 1 January 2025. Charged per unit, not per person.
Rome4 EUR (1-star) to 10 EUR (5-star) per person per night; flat 6 EUR for short-term rentalsCapped at 10 nights.
SantoriniClimate resilience tax 2 EUR (1-2 star) to 15 EUR (5-star) per nightHigh season only, April through October.
VancouverCombined 5.5% municipal accommodation tax (3% MRDT + 2.5% Major Events MRDT)The extra 2.5% runs through 31 January 2030 to help fund World Cup costs.
ViennaOrtstaxe 5% of the room rate from 1 July 2026 (up from 3.2%)A further rise to 8% is scheduled for 1 July 2027.

Not a hotel tax, still on the bill

Venice charges a day-tripper access fee on 60 days between April and July 2026: 5 EUR if you book more than three days ahead, 10 EUR inside that window, 08:30 to 16:00. Overnight guests and residents are exempt. That is a gate fee, not an overnight tax. The full calendar is in our Venice access fee 2026 note.

London is developing an overnight visitor levy under the English Devolution and Community Empowerment Bill, floated at either 2 to 4 pounds per person per night or about 5% of the room. It is not in force. Do not budget it as a current tax.

How to actually budget it

Percentage taxes (Amsterdam, Berlin, Edinburgh, Hong Kong, Vancouver, Vienna, Kyoto's bands) scale with the room. A 200 EUR net night in Amsterdam is about 25 EUR in tourist tax before the 21% VAT. Flat per-person taxes (Lisbon, Porto, Barcelona's surcharge, Milan, Rome) scale with the number of people and the number of nights, then usually cap. A family of four in Lisbon for a week hits the 7-night cap at 112 EUR. That is not a rounding error.

Booking sites sometimes collect the tax and sometimes do not. Assume it is extra until the confirmation says otherwise. For the destination-level version of these numbers, including the tickets and scams that sit next to the tax, start at the city page rather than this table.

posts.title: Venice access fee 2026: 60 days, 5 or 10 euros, overnight guests exempt
posts.summary: The 2026 contributo di accesso runs 60 days between April and July. Book more than three days out and it is 5 euros. Inside that window it is 10. Overnight guests do not pay it.
posts.body:
Venice is not charging you to look at the water. It is charging day-trippers to walk into the historic centre on the days the city has decided it cannot absorb another surge. In 2026 that calendar is the largest the scheme has used.

When the fee applies in 2026

The contributo di accesso applies on 60 days between April and July: every Friday, Saturday and Sunday from 3 April through 26 July, plus 6 April, the week beginning 27 April, and the week beginning 1 June. It is enforced from 08:30 to 16:00. Arrive as a day-tripper on one of those days, in that window, and you owe it.

What it costs

5 euros if you book more than three days ahead. 10 euros if you buy inside the three-day window. In 2025, 49% of the people who paid paid the higher rate. That is not a trivia statistic, it is the default outcome for anyone who treats the fee as a walk-up ticket.

Residents and overnight guests are exempt. Overnight guests still register. If you are already paying for a hotel night in the city, the fee is not stacked on top. Two separate day trips, on two fee days, with two last-minute 10 euro payments, is the expensive version of Venice. One overnight stay is usually cheaper in total.

Has it reduced the crowds?

Not in any way a visitor will notice. In 2025 the scheme collected 5,421,425 euros from 723,497 payments, nearly double 2024's 2.4 million euros from 485,062 payments across a 29-day run. The historic centre is down to 47,995 residents. Peak day-tripper counts have been put as high as 85,000. The fee raised money. It did not restore a quiet city.

Around San Marco the other costs are worse than the fee: restaurant overcharging is systematic, a single vaporetto ride is 9.50 euros, and gondola prices above the posted association rate are a documented pattern. The 5 euro access fee is the line item that is trivial to get right and embarrassing to get wrong.

Book it when you book the train. The destination page and the Venice 2026 guide cover the rest of the bill.

posts.title: Park Guell ticket price 2026: 18 euros after an 80 percent jump
posts.summary: Park Guell adult admission is 18 euros in 2026, up from 10 euros, capped at 1,400 visitors an hour. Sagrada Familia is 26 euros, or 36 with towers, plus a centenary surcharge from June through December.
posts.body:
Barcelona's two most famous Gaudi sites both got more expensive in 2026, and neither is a walk-up anymore.

Park Guell

Adult admission is 18 euros, an 80% jump from 10 euros at the start of 2026. Entry is capped at 1,400 visitors per hour on a timed ticket. Book online days ahead. Showing up at the gate in July is how you spend an afternoon in Barcelona not seeing Park Guell.

Sagrada Familia

A standard ticket with audio guide is 26 euros in 2026. Tower access is 36 euros. A centenary surcharge of 2 to 5 euros applies from June through December 2026. Timed entry is mandatory. This is also not a walk-up.

The rest of the 2026 Barcelona bill

The tourist tax effectively doubled on 1 April 2026: 4.50 EUR Catalan regional rate plus 5 EUR city surcharge per person per night, plus 10% VAT. Five-star stays land around 12 EUR per person per night in tax alone. Short-term rentals are about 9.50 EUR. The city surcharge keeps climbing 1 EUR a year through 2029, and every remaining tourist-apartment licence is set to expire by November 2028.

Transit is still the cheap line: a T-Casual 10-ride card is 13 euros in one zone. That does not offset an 8 euro Park Guell increase plus a doubled hotel tax plus a Sagrada surcharge, but it is the one 2026 number in Barcelona that barely moved.

Full context, including pickpocketing hotspots on Metro Lines 1 and 3 and the Airbnb countdown, is on the Barcelona destination page and the 2026 Barcelona guide.

posts.title: Amsterdam tourist tax 2026: 12.5 percent plus 21 percent VAT
posts.summary: Amsterdam charges Europe's highest tourist tax at 12.5 percent of the net room rate, stacked on a 21 percent VAT that took effect 1 January 2026. The coalition plans 16 percent in 2027.
posts.body:
Amsterdam is no longer a cheap city that happens to have a canal tax. In 2026 the overnight bill is a 12.5 percent tourist tax, already the highest in Europe, stacked on Dutch VAT on hotel accommodation that jumped from 9 percent to 21 percent on 1 January 2026. On a 200 euro net room, the tourist tax is about 25 euros before VAT. Together they take roughly a third of the quoted rate.

What you pay in 2026

The tourist tax is 12.5 percent of the net room price, per night. It is a percentage, so it scales with the hotel. The VAT change is national, not an Amsterdam extra, but it lands on the same line. The new municipal coalition has said it plans to raise the tourist tax from 12.5 percent to 16 percent in 2027, and later toward 20 percent. That is a plan, not the current rate. Budget 12.5 percent plus 21 percent VAT now.

Why the city is doing this

Amsterdam logged 23.7 million overnight stays in 2025, about 800,000 more than 2024, while running the Stay Away campaign against stag-party search traffic. A citywide hotel bed freeze has been in effect since November 2024. From 1 April 2026, short-term holiday rentals in the city centre and De Pijp are capped at 15 nights a year. Ocean cruise dockings are capped at 100 per year from 2026. None of that reduced demand enough to drop the tax.

What else hits the same trip

Anne Frank House tickets are 16.50 euros for adults in 2026, 7 euros for ages 10-17, and they release every Tuesday at 10:00 Amsterdam time, six weeks ahead. Popular midday slots have been reported gone in two to three minutes. A GVB 24-hour transit ticket is 10 euros; OVpay GVB Max caps the day at 10.50 euros. Bike rental from a reputable shop is 12 to 18 euros a day, and the city estimates around 28,500 actual bike thefts a year.

The Amsterdam destination page and the Amsterdam 2026 guide cover Red Light District rules (100 euro outdoor cannabis fine, no photos of windows). Compare the tax against other cities in the 2026 tourist tax table.

posts.title: Kyoto lodging tax 2026: five tiers, up to 10,000 yen per person per night
posts.summary: From 1 March 2026 Kyoto charges a five-tier lodging tax per person per night, from 200 yen under 6,000 yen rooms to 10,000 yen at 100,000 yen and above. The top band is the steepest in Japan.
posts.body:
Kyoto restructured its lodging tax on 1 March 2026. It is charged per person, per night, not per room, and the top band is the steepest lodging tax in Japan. A couple in a 120,000 yen room is 20,000 yen of tax for that night, on top of the room.

The five tiers, from 1 March 2026

Room rate bandTax per person per night
Under 6,000 yen200 yen
6,000 to 19,999 yen400 yen
20,000 to 49,999 yen1,000 yen
50,000 to 99,999 yen4,000 yen
100,000 yen and above10,000 yen

Golden Week 2026 already showed what the top of the market looks like: Kyoto had the highest average hotel rate among six major Japanese cities at 48,900 yen. That is the 1,000 yen band for most rooms, 4,000 yen once you cross 50,000.

The rest of the 2026 squeeze

Kyoto drew 10.88 million foreign visitors in 2024. The 700 yen bus-only day pass is gone. The city-bus central-zone flat fare is 230 yen; the sightseeing limited express buses (EX100/EX101) are 500 yen adult. A Subway and Bus 1-Day Pass is 1,100 yen. Resident-priority bus pricing (about 200 yen for residents versus 350-400 yen for visitors) is announced for fiscal 2027, not in force yet.

The sites themselves are still cheap: Kinkaku-ji and Kiyomizu-dera are 500 yen for adults, Fushimi Inari is free and always open. Gion is the opposite of cheap if you ignore the signs: private alleys off Hanamikoji Street carry a 10,000 yen trespass fine.

Full planning notes are on the Kyoto destination page and the Kyoto 2026 trip planner. City-by-city comparison: 2026 tourist taxes.

posts.title: Edinburgh visitor levy 2026: 5 percent, first five nights, first in the UK
posts.summary: Edinburgh became the first UK city to charge a visitor levy on 24 July 2026: 5 percent on paid overnight accommodation for the first five consecutive nights. It applies to bookings made on or after 1 October 2025.
posts.body:
Edinburgh is the first UK city to put a visitor levy on the hotel bill. From 24 July 2026 it is 5 percent of paid overnight accommodation, charged on the first five consecutive nights of a stay, and projected to raise up to 50 million pounds a year. Bookings made before 1 October 2025 are exempt even if the trip itself is later. Bookings made on or after that date are not.

How the 5 percent actually works

It is a percentage of the room, not a flat per-person fee. A 200 pound night is 10 pounds of levy. Five nights is the cap: night six and after in the same stay do not add more levy. A one-night stay pays 5 percent once. A Fringe-week booking at 300 pounds a night for five nights is 75 pounds of levy on top of an already doubled or tripled room rate.

August is the real multiplier

The Edinburgh Festival Fringe runs 7 to 31 August 2026. Festival-month hostels run about 45 to 80 pounds for a dorm against 20 to 35 pounds in a normal month. Budget hotels 150 to 300 pounds against 55 to 140. Mid-range 250 to 500 against 140 to 280. The levy sits on top of that, it does not replace it. January to March and November are the 20 to 40 percent cheaper window.

Other 2026 line items

UK ETA for non-British/Irish visitors without UK immigration status is required from 25 February 2026. The fee rose from 16 to 20 pounds on 8 April 2026, valid up to two years, no child discount. Lothian Buses adult singles rose to 2.20 pounds on 22 February 2026. Edinburgh Trams airport-to-city is 7.90 pounds one way, frozen for 2026. Edinburgh Castle is about 21.50 to 23.50 pounds online, cheaper than the gate, on 30-minute timed slots.

The Royal Mile is one of the most complained-about tourist traps in the UK. Police Scotland logged 47 tourist-related thefts in 2025, down from 62 in 2024. Violent crime against visitors is rare. The levy is the new line item; the Fringe calendar is still the one that can actually ruin the budget.

More on the Edinburgh destination page and the 2026 Edinburgh guide. Compare other cities in the 2026 tourist tax table.

posts.title: Anne Frank House tickets 2026: 16.50 euros, Tuesday 10:00 release, timed entry only
posts.summary: Adult tickets are 16.50 euros including the booking fee. They release every Tuesday at 10:00 Amsterdam time, six weeks ahead. Walk-up is not a real option.
posts.body:
Anne Frank House is the one Amsterdam ticket you cannot treat as a same-day decision. Entry is timed and online only. Adults pay 16.50 euros, ages 10 to 17 pay 7 euros, and ages 0 to 9 pay 1 euro. Each of those prices already includes a 1 euro booking fee.

How tickets actually release

Tickets go on sale every Tuesday at 10:00 Amsterdam time, for dates six weeks ahead. Popular midday slots have been reported gone in two to three minutes. That is why the destination page says to book this before you book the hotel. An early slot is the practical one: the annexe has steep stairs, small rooms, and no spare capacity for people who arrived late and hoped.

What does not discount it

The I amsterdam Card gives no discount. Museumkaart and ICOM cardholders still pay the 1 euro booking fee. An EYC card is 7 euros. Third-party platforms are not how this museum sells, and treating them as a backup when the official sale is sold out is how people buy a useless PDF.

The rest of the Amsterdam bill

This ticket is cheap next to the room. Amsterdam's tourist tax is 12.5 percent of the net rate, stacked on 21 percent VAT from 1 January 2026. Details: Amsterdam tourist tax 2026. The house itself is at Anne Frank House on the Amsterdam destination page.

posts.title: Sagrada Familia tickets 2026: 26 euros, 36 with towers, timed entry, now finished
posts.summary: Basilica entry is 26 euros, 36 with towers. Timed slots, 30 minutes of grace. A centenary surcharge of 2 to 5 euros applies June through December 2026. Book on the official site.
posts.body:
The Sagrada Familia is structurally complete in 2026: the upper arm of the cross on the Tower of Jesus Christ went on 20 February 2026, at 172.5 metres the tallest church in the world. The ticket is priced like it knows that.

Official 2026 prices

TicketPrice
Basilica26 euros
Basilica with towers36 euros
Seniors21 euros, or 28 with towers
Under-30s and students with card24 euros, or 34 with towers
Guided tour30 euros at the base rate

Disabled visitors and their companions pay only for additional services; general entrance is free. Entry is timed, with 30 minutes of grace after the time on the ticket. Towers are a separate product and sell out first. A centenary surcharge of 2 to 5 euros applies from June through December 2026.

How to not miss it

Book on the official site before you book the hotel. Morning light and late-afternoon light hit opposite sides of the nave, so the slot you pick changes the building. Walk-up is a gamble now that the basilica is finished and on every 2026 itinerary.

Park Guell jumped 80 percent to 18 euros the same year: Park Guell ticket price 2026. The hotel tax doubled on 1 April 2026: Barcelona tourist tax 2026. Place page: Sagrada Familia. City: Barcelona.

posts.title: Barcelona tourist tax 2026: 4.50 euros plus 5 euro city surcharge, still climbing
posts.summary: From 1 April 2026 Barcelona adds a 4.50 euro Catalan rate plus a 5 euro city surcharge per person per night, plus 10 percent VAT. Five-star stays land around 12 euros each. The city surcharge rises 1 euro a year through 2029.
posts.body:
Barcelona's tourist tax effectively doubled at the top of the market on 1 April 2026. It is a combined 4.50 euro Catalan regional rate plus a 5 euro Barcelona municipal surcharge, per person, per night, plus 10 percent VAT on top of that.

What a night actually adds

Stay typeAbout, per person per night
Five-star hotel12 euros (up from 7.50 euros in 2025)
Four-star hotel8.40 euros
Short-term rental9.50 euros
Cruise passengerup to 11 euros, depending on how long the ship is docked

The Barcelona portion of the surcharge is scheduled to rise another euro a year through 2029. This is not a one-off 2026 bump.

The rental supply is shrinking at the same time

Every remaining tourist-apartment licence is set to expire by November 2028. The city has been catching about 300 illegal listings a month. Fines for operating without a licence can reach 600,000 euros. Budget travellers who planned on an apartment are working against a shrinking, enforced pool, not a loophole.

Tickets moved too

Park Guell is 18 euros, up 80 percent from 10. Sagrada Familia is 26 euros, 36 with towers, plus a June-December centenary surcharge. Transit is the cheap line: a T-Casual 10-ride card is 13 euros in one zone.

Ticket notes: Sagrada Familia tickets 2026, Park Guell 18 euros. City page: Barcelona. Other cities: 2026 tourist tax table.

posts.title: Manaus 2026: opera in the jungle, the Meeting of the Waters, and how to do the Amazon right
posts.summary: Manaus is the Amazon's real city: two million people, a gilded Teatro Amazonas, and the Negro and Solimoes running side by side without mixing. It rewards travelers who plan health, tours, and transport in advance.
posts.body:
Manaus is not a beach town with a jungle day trip bolted on. It is a working Amazon city of about two million people, with an opera house that still looks impossible, and the rainforest starting where the pavement stops. That combination is the reason to go.

What is actually great

Teatro Amazonas is the postcard that is not a scam. Built during the rubber boom and still in use, it is the one city-center sight worth a ticket, commonly around 30 reals for a tour. Thirty minutes downstream, the Meeting of the Waters is the real trick of geography: the dark Rio Negro and the milky Solimoes run side by side for kilometres before they mix. Day boats from the city make that trip routinely.

The jungle is why most people fly here. A reputable two or three night lodge from Manaus typically runs in the hundreds of dollars per person, not tens. That is the honest price of a boat, a guide, and a bed that is not a dock tout's WhatsApp. Book before you land. Eduardo Gomes International Airport (MAO) is well secured; the risk is the arrivals hall, where unlicensed taxis and informal guides close in. Walk past them. Uber, 99, and the official taxi kiosk all work. Airport to Ponta Negra is often in the 10 to 16 US dollar range on an app.

Health and the part that can ruin it

Yellow fever vaccination is strongly recommended for Amazonas even though Brazil does not always demand the card at the border. Dengue, chikungunya, and malaria risk exist in the basin. This is the Brazilian city that most rewards a travel clinic visit before you buy the lodge.

Brazil sits at US Level 2, exercise increased caution. In Manaus the tourist core is Ponta Negra, Adrianopolis, and the Teatro Amazonas area. After dark, use apps door to door. Petty theft and phone snatching are the practical crimes, not a reason to skip the opera house. Cheap last-minute jungle deals with no website are the other failure mode.

US, Canadian, and Australian visitors should check Brazil's current e-visa rules before flying. The city page is Manaus.

posts.title: Rio de Janeiro 2026: the views still earn it, and the South Zone is safer than the reputation
posts.summary: Christ the Redeemer and Sugarloaf still deliver. Ipanema and Leblon posted zero homicides in Q1 2026, violent crime is down for a third straight year, and the beaches, food, and music are not a myth.
posts.body:
Rio de Janeiro is still one of the most beautiful cities on earth. That is not marketing. Corcovado with Christ the Redeemer, the Bondinho up Sugarloaf, Ipanema in late light, and a Saturday feijoada are the reasons people keep coming back, and they are still good in 2026.

What improved

Violent lethality in Rio was down 12 percent in the first quarter of 2026 versus a year earlier, part of a third straight year of falling violent crime citywide. Ipanema and Leblon recorded zero homicides in that quarter. In May 2026 the city added 61 municipal guard officers for round-the-clock patrol of the Copacabana, Ipanema, and Leblon corridor, the largest such push since the 2016 Olympics. Base yourself in Ipanema or Leblon if that data matters to you. The food and the beach do not get worse when you move one neighborhood west of Copacabana.

Tickets and timing

Christ the Redeemer is a booked slot, not a wander-up. Van plus entry runs roughly 108 reals in low season to 168 in high season. Sugarloaf's two-stage cable car is about 170 reals round trip for an adult. Go a few hours before sunset and skip the 280 to 350 real VIP packages unless you want the glass of sparkling wine.

Carnival 2027 is February 5 through 13. Hotel rooms that sit around 400 reals most of the year have been quoted at 1,200 to 2,000 that week. Go then only if you want Carnival. The rest of the year, Rio is still a city where the views and the music are cheap relative to what they are.

Be straight about Copacabana

Copacabana robberies rose about 25 percent and thefts about 56 percent from 2024 to 2025. Phone theft is a citywide problem. Keep the phone away on the beachfront between 10pm and 2am. Brazil remains US Level 2. None of that cancels Sugarloaf. It tells you which six blocks to treat with respect. Full notes: Rio de Janeiro and the Rio guide.

posts.title: Tehran is a great city. Most Western governments currently say do not go.
posts.summary: Tehran has mountains, one of the great bazaars, and a food culture that deserves the reputation. The US, UK, Canada, and Australia all advise against travel to Iran in 2026. This is not a packing list.
posts.body:
Tehran is a real capital: more than nine million people against the Alborz, with the Grand Bazaar, museum collections, and a food scene that travelers who have been there talk about for years. The city is not a desert outpost. It is a mountain-backed metropolis with ski slopes a short drive north and one of the densest urban cultures in the region.

What is worth saying out loud

The architecture of the twentieth century, from Azadi Tower to the museum circuit, is distinctive. Iranian cooking, from kebabs to tahdig to the sweet shops, is not a sideshow. The bazaar is a working market, not a staged souk. People who know the city describe hospitality that is specific and memorable. Those things are true whether or not you can go this year.

The 2026 advisory is not a vibe

The US State Department lists Iran as Level 4, Do Not Travel, citing terrorism, unrest, kidnapping, arbitrary arrest of US citizens, and wrongful detention. There is no US embassy in Tehran. The UK FCDO advises against all travel. Canada and Australia say the same. Dual nationals have been detained. That is the current official picture as of 2026, not a leftover from a different decade.

RuinMyTrip will not publish a 2026 itinerary that pretends those advisories are optional color. If you hold a Western passport, this is not a leisure booking. If you have family there or another reason to follow the city, read travel.state.gov and the FCDO page yourself. The destination page is Tehran.

posts.title: Buzios 2026: 23 beaches, three hours from Rio, still the easy one
posts.summary: Armação dos Búzios, often spelled Buzios, is the peninsula east of Rio with 23 beaches, Orla Bardot, and a bus from Novo Rio that still starts around 19 US dollars. It is the Brazilian beach town that is actually simple.
posts.body:
If you meant Bouziou, the place is Buzios: Armação dos Búzios, a 71 square kilometre peninsula about 170 kilometres east of Rio de Janeiro. Brigitte Bardot's 1964 visit is the origin story, and it is not a myth. The town is still small, still about beaches, and still the easiest coastal reset after Rio.

Why it works

Twenty-three beaches sit on an eight kilometre peninsula. Geriba is the surf beach. Azeda and Azedinha are the calm coves. Joao Fernandes is the postcard. Rua das Pedras and Orla Bardot are the evening walk. Schooner trips along the coast are the default afternoon, commonly in the 20 to 40 US dollar range for a couple of hours. You can walk a lot of it. Cooperative vans along Avenida Jose Bento Ribeiro Dantas are about 5 reals if you wave them down.

How to get there

Skip the tiny general-aviation airstrip unless you have a reason. Fly into Rio (GIG or SDU), then take Autoviacao 1001 from Rodoviaria Novo Rio. The ride is about 3 hours 10 minutes to 3 hours 50 minutes. Recent one-way fares have been in the 19 to 32 US dollar range. Driving is about three hours depending on traffic out of the city.

Winter (June to September) is drier and milder. Shoulder months are quieter and cheaper. January through March is heat, rain, and Brazilian holiday prices. Pair it with Rio. City page: Buzios.

posts.title: San Francisco 2026: the city is busy again, and the views never left
posts.summary: SF Travel forecasts 24.2 million visitors and 9.9 billion dollars in spending for 2026, beating the 2019 record. The Golden Gate, the hills, and the food are still the reason. The hotel tax is 14 percent.
posts.body:
San Francisco is a great city that had a rough few years and is booking again. Mayor Lurie's office and SF Travel put 2026 at 24.2 million visitors and 9.9 billion dollars in spending, above the 2019 record. 2025 already brought 23.7 million people and 9.4 billion dollars. The Golden Gate, the grid of hills, Golden Gate Park, and the food in the Mission and Chinatown did not go anywhere.

What to actually do

Walk a steep neighborhood instead of only Fisherman's Wharf. Ride a cable car once because it is the real 19th century machine, then use Muni for the rest. Book Alcatraz the minute your dates are firm: it is a National Park Service site sold only through Alcatraz City Cruises, it is not on CityPASS, and day tickets in 2026 run about 47 to 51 dollars for adults and sell out weeks ahead. September and October are the warmest stretch, the local Indian summer.

What it costs

The hotel tax is 14 percent TOT on stays under 30 days, plus a Tourism Improvement District assessment of 2.00 to 2.25 percent depending on zone. Average daily hotel rate in the 2026 forecast is about 258 dollars before those add-ons. Cable cars are 9 dollars a ride in 2026, rising to 12 in January 2027. A Clipper tap or contactless card works on Muni, BART, and the cars.

Street theft, especially phones, is still the practical nuisance. Keep it put away on transit and in crowds. The city is worth the hill. More: hotel tax, Alcatraz tickets, cable car fares, San Francisco.

posts.title: San Francisco hotel tax 2026: 14 percent TOT plus 2 to 2.25 percent TID
posts.summary: San Francisco charges a 14 percent transient occupancy tax on stays under 30 days. Hotels also pass on a Tourism Improvement District assessment of 2.25 percent in Zone 1 and 2.00 percent in Zone 2.
posts.body:
San Francisco's hotel bill is not the rate you saw on the booking site. The city imposes a 14 percent transient occupancy tax on the rental of accommodations for less than 30 consecutive nights. Hotel operators and short-term rental hosts collect it and remit it to the Treasurer and Tax Collector. That rate is in the Business and Tax Regulation Code and is the figure in the city's own TOT pages and FY 2025-26 budget documents.

The extra line

On top of TOT, many properties add a Tourism Improvement District assessment: 2.25 percent in Zone 1 and 2.00 percent in Zone 2. Those can appear as a separate folio line. Together with 14 percent, a 300 dollar net night is not a 300 dollar night.

Hotel tax is a real slice of the city's budget: the FY 2025-26 original budget for hotel tax was about 298 million dollars, with FY 2026-27 budgeted around 312 million, still at 14 percent. SF Travel's 2026 visitor forecast puts average daily rate near 258 dollars, occupancy near 69 percent.

City page: San Francisco. Broader 2026 costs: San Francisco 2026.

posts.title: Alcatraz tickets 2026: about 47 to 51 dollars, not on any city pass, book early
posts.summary: Alcatraz is a National Park Service site. Tickets are sold only through Alcatraz City Cruises. Adult day tours run about 47 to 51 dollars in 2026. CityPASS, Go City, and C3 do not include it.
posts.body:
Alcatraz is the one San Francisco ticket people still underestimate. It is not a hop-on ferry. It is a timed National Park Service visit sold exclusively through Alcatraz City Cruises from Pier 33. Adult day-tour tickets in 2026 run approximately 47 to 51 dollars, including the round-trip ferry and the audio tour. Night tours cost more and sell out first.

What is not included

No San Francisco city pass covers Alcatraz. Not CityPASS, not Go City, not C3. If a third-party site is selling you a combo that looks like Alcatraz plus a pass, read the fine print. Book the official product when your dates are firm, often weeks ahead in summer and October.

The island is why you came: the cellhouse, the bay, the city skyline on the way back. Pair it with a day that does not also try to do Muir Woods and wine country. San Francisco.

posts.title: San Francisco cable car fare 2026: 9 dollars now, 12 dollars in January 2027
posts.summary: A single cable car ride is 9 dollars in 2026. SFMTA's adopted budget raises it to 12 dollars in January 2027 and phases out three- and seven-day cable car tickets in favor of an 18 dollar all-day Muni pass.
posts.body:
San Francisco's cable cars are not a theme-park ride. They are a working 19th century system on three lines: Powell-Hyde, Powell-Mason, and California Street. In 2026 a single ride is 9 dollars, paid in cash, Clipper, MuniMobile, or a contactless card. Seniors and disabled riders pay 9 dollars from 7am to 9pm and 4 dollars from 9pm to 7am.

What changes in 2027

The San Francisco Municipal Transportation Agency budget raises a single cable car ride from 9 dollars to 12 dollars in January 2027. Three-day and seven-day cable car tickets go away. The replacement is an 18 dollar cable-car-plus day pass that covers all Muni, with two children free with an adult. That is a tourist product. If you are riding once for the hill, ride it in 2026 at 9 dollars or budget 12 later.

For getting around, tap Clipper or a contactless credit card on Muni, BART, and the cars. Do the Powell-Hyde line once for the view down to the bay, then walk. San Francisco.

posts.title: Accra tourism levy 2026: 1 percent on hotels, restaurants and tours
posts.summary: Ghana adds a 1 percent tourism levy to hotel, restaurant and tour bills in Accra in 2026, according to the Ghana Tourism Authority. On a 7,200 cedi trip that is 72 cedis.
posts.body:
Visitors to Accra pay a 1 percent tourism levy on hotel bills, restaurant bills and other licensed tourism services in 2026. The figure comes from the Ghana Tourism Authority itself, whose Tourism Development Fund page calls it a one per cent tourism levy, payable by a patron of a tourism enterprise, and charged on the net cost of service or products purchased.

Who collects it

The same page says an operator must be licensed and certified to act as an agent of the authority before it can collect the levy and pay it into the fund. It lists the businesses in scope as hotels, guest houses, serviced apartments, restaurants, drinking bars, night clubs, car rental firms, tour operators, conference and banqueting facilities, spas, cinemas and tourist sites. An operator collects for a month and then has a further 30 days to hand the money over, which is why the line appears on your bill rather than at any border.

What a stay costs with the levy applied

Take four nights in an Accra hotel at 1,500 cedis per night. The room total is 6,000 cedis and the levy on it is 60 cedis. Add three restaurant meals at 400 cedis each and the levy on those is 12 cedis. On a 7,200 cedi trip the tourism levy comes to 72 cedis, a small line next to the other statutory charges that appear on a Ghanaian folio.

What is still unclear

The authority's page does not publish a worked example or say how the levy sits alongside the other taxes on an invoice, so the exact cedi figure on your bill can differ slightly from the simple calculation above.

Sources: ghana.travel, ghana.travel.

posts.title: Banff park pass 2026: 12.25 dollars per adult per day, free until September 7
posts.summary: Parks Canada lists a 12.25 dollar adult day pass and a 24.50 dollar family pass for Banff in 2026, with entry free until September 7 under the Canada Strong Pass.
posts.body:
Banff National Park charges 12.25 dollars per adult for a daily pass in 2026, according to the fee page Parks Canada publishes for the park itself. Seniors pay 10.75 dollars, youth aged 17 and under enter free, and a family or group travelling in one vehicle pays 24.50 dollars for the day.

The free window in 2026

The same page states that the Canada Strong Pass with Parks Canada ends September 7, 2026, and that from September 8 visitors are required to buy a valid daily park pass or an annual Discovery Pass. Entry to Banff therefore costs nothing up to that date and returns to the posted rates the day after, which matters if your trip straddles the changeover.

Day pass or annual pass

The Discovery Pass on the same page is 83.50 dollars for an adult, 71.50 dollars for a senior and 167.50 dollars for a family or group. For a family driving in after September 8, six separate days at 24.50 dollars comes to 147 dollars, still under the annual pass. A seventh day takes the total to 171.50 dollars, so the Discovery Pass is the cheaper option from the seventh day of entry onward.

What is still unclear

The fee page does not say whether the 2026 daily rates carry into 2027, so anyone planning a trip past this year should read it again before budgeting.

Sources: parks.canada.ca, parks.canada.ca.

posts.title: Bangkok Grand Palace entry 2026: 500 baht per foreign visitor
posts.summary: The Grand Palace's own site puts admission at 500 baht in 2026, with tickets sold only until 3:30 PM. Two adults pay 1,000 baht for the single largest fixed cost of a first sightseeing day.
posts.body:
Admission to the Grand Palace in Bangkok is 500 baht a head in 2026. The figure comes from the palace's own website, which states that tickets are sold from 8:30 AM to 3:30 PM and cost 500 baht, and which says the ticket gives access to Wat Phra Kaew, the temple of the Emerald Buddha, inside the same walls.

Hours and timing

The site gives daily opening as 8:30 AM to 4:30 PM, with the ticket window closing a full hour earlier at 3:30 PM. Arriving in the late afternoon therefore means no entry that day even though the grounds themselves are still open, which is the single most common way visitors waste the trip across town.

What a sightseeing day costs

Two adults visiting the Grand Palace pay 1,000 baht between them. A group of four adults pays 2,000 baht. Because the charge is a flat per person ticket rather than a nightly or percentage tax, it does not scale with how long you stay in Bangkok or what your hotel costs.

What is still unclear

Thailand has discussed a nationwide arrival fee for foreign visitors for several years, and no official page consulted for this article confirms a start date or an amount in force during 2026, so any figure circulating for it should be treated as unconfirmed.

Sources: royalgrandpalace.th, royalgrandpalace.th.

posts.title: Berlin city tax 2026: 7.5 percent of the net room price
posts.summary: Berlin's accommodation tax is 7.5 percent in 2026, per the Senate Department for Finance. Four nights at 130 euros adds 39 euros of city tax.
posts.body:
Berlin charges an overnight accommodation tax of 7.5 percent in 2026. The rate comes from the Senate Department for Finance, whose tax FAQ records that the rate was raised to 7.5 percent and applies the tax to paid overnight stays in the city.

What changes in 2026

The same FAQ lists three changes taking effect on January 1, 2026. The taxation and filing period becomes the calendar quarter only, the 10 bed threshold that kept the smallest guest houses outside the tax is dropped, and electronic filing of the return becomes compulsory. All three land on the accommodation business rather than on the guest, but the second one quietly widens the number of Berlin properties where the charge shows up on a bill at all.

A worked example

Four nights in a Berlin hotel at 130 euros a night is 520 euros of room charges. At 7.5 percent the city tax on that stay is 39 euros. A full week at the same rate, 910 euros of room charges, carries 68.25 euros of tax. The charge is a percentage rather than a flat nightly amount, so it rises with the room rate rather than with the number of people in the room.

What is still unclear

The FAQ page consulted here does not spell out exactly which parts of a booking make up the taxable amount, so whether a rate that bundles breakfast is taxed in full is not answered there.

Sources: berlin.de, berlin.de.

posts.title: Budapest tourism tax 2026: 4 percent of the gross room price in District V
posts.summary: Central Budapest charges a 4 percent tourism tax on the gross room price in 2026, while District XVI charges a flat 400 forints per person per night. Three nights at 60,000 forints adds 7,200 forints.
posts.body:
A hotel guest in central Budapest pays a tourism tax of 4 percent of the gross accommodation price in 2026. The rate is published by the District V local government, whose tax page states that the base is the accommodation fee for the guest nights begun and that the rate is 4 percent of the gross accommodation fee.

The rate depends on the district

Budapest sets this tax district by district rather than city wide, so the method changes as you cross the map. District XVI publishes a flat charge instead, stating on its own tax page that the tax is 400 forints per person per guest night with effect from January 1, 2026. Two people in that outer district pay a fixed 800 forints a night, while the same pair in an expensive District V hotel pay a percentage that climbs with the room rate.

A worked example

Three nights in a District V hotel at 60,000 forints gross per night is 180,000 forints of room charges, and the 4 percent tourism tax on that is 7,200 forints. The same three nights for two guests in District XVI would carry 2,400 forints of tax, because the flat rate is charged per person rather than per room.

What is still unclear

Neither district page consulted here lists every Budapest district in one table, so a traveller booking outside District V has to check that district's own tax page to learn which of the two methods applies.

Sources: belvaros-lipotvaros.hu, bp16.hu.

posts.title: Buenos Aires tourist tax 2026: 1.50 US dollars per night per foreign visitor
posts.summary: The city's own tourism site puts the Derecho de Uso Urbano at 1.50 US dollars per night for foreign visitors over 12 in 2026. Two people for six nights pay 18 dollars at check out.
posts.body:
Foreign visitors staying in the city of Buenos Aires pay 1.50 US dollars per night in 2026. The city government's own tourism page on the Derecho de Uso Urbano states that every foreign tourist over 12 years old pays a rate of 1.50 dollars for each night, and that the charge has applied since Law 6278 took effect on March 1, 2020.

How it is collected

The same page says the amount is charged when you check out, worked out from the type of accommodation and the number of nights, and paid using whatever method the property accepts. It applies across hotels, boutique hotels, apart hotels, temporary rentals and cruises, so a short term apartment booking is treated the same way as a hotel room. Nobody collects it at the airport.

A worked example

Two adults staying six nights in Palermo pay 1.50 dollars each per night, which is 18 dollars added at check out on top of the room rate. A family of two adults and one teenager over 12 staying ten nights pays 45 dollars. Because it is a flat per person amount, it weighs far more heavily on a cheap hostel bill than on a five star one.

What is still unclear

The page names no exemption beyond the age limit and does not say how the dollar figure is converted for a peso bill, so the exact amount charged at check out depends on the rate your accommodation applies that day.

Sources: turismo.buenosaires.gob.ar, turismo.buenosaires.gob.ar.

posts.title: Cancun visitor tax 2026: 2.50 UMA, which is 293.28 pesos per foreign visitor
posts.summary: Quintana Roo law sets the foreign visitor charge at 2.50 UMA, and INEGI fixed the 2026 daily UMA at 117.31 pesos, so the 2026 figure is 293.28 pesos per person.
posts.body:
Every foreign visitor entering Quintana Roo, the Mexican state that contains Cancun, owes a state charge of 2.50 UMA, which works out at 293.28 pesos in 2026. Article 51 Octies of the Ley de Derechos del Estado de Quintana Roo sets that tariff for the use or enjoyment of state public domain property, and INEGI, the national statistics institute, fixed the daily UMA at 117.31 pesos with effect from February 1, 2026.

Who is exempt

The same article exempts foreign visitors who enter Quintana Roo across the southern border of the state. Article 51 Nonies charges cruise passengers a separate five US dollar right, collected by the shipping line at the moment the ticket is sold, and states that paying it releases those passengers from the charge in Article 51 Octies. The state collects the visitor charge through its own official portal at visitax.gob.mx.

A worked example

A family of four flying into Cancun in 2026 owes four times 293.28 pesos, or 1,173.12 pesos. Two travellers owe 586.56 pesos. The charge is per person and per entry rather than per night, so a two week stay and a three night stay cost exactly the same.

What is still unclear

The law fixes the tariff in UMA and the official payment portal does not publish a peso amount on its public pages, so the figure the portal actually charges may not match the UMA calculation to the centavo.

Sources: uqroo.mx, uqroo.mx, inegi.org.mx, visitax.gob.mx.

posts.title: Cape Town Table Mountain cableway 2026: 475 rand return online, 530 at the ticket office
posts.summary: The cableway's own price list puts an adult return at 475 rand online and 530 rand at the ticket office, valid from 1 July 2026. A family of four saves 190 rand by booking online.
posts.body:
A return ride on the Table Mountain cableway costs 475 rand for an adult booking online and 530 rand for an adult buying at the ticket office. Both figures come from the cableway's own ticket page, which marks the price list as valid from 1 July 2026 to 30 June 2027.

The full price list

Online, an adult one way ticket is 300 rand, and a child aged 4 to 17 pays 230 rand return or 165 rand one way. At the ticket office the same tickets are 330 rand for an adult one way, 270 rand for a child return and 180 rand for a child one way. Booking online therefore saves 55 rand on an adult return and 40 rand on a child return, before you count the time saved.

A worked example

Two adults and two children riding up and down pay 475 plus 475 plus 230 plus 230, or 1,410 rand, when booked online. The same four tickets bought at the ticket office come to 1,600 rand, so a family pays 190 rand more for turning up without a booking. The cableway also warns that an online ticket still does not remove the queue on a busy day.

What is still unclear

This price list covers the cable car only. The conservation fee that South African National Parks charges for parts of Table Mountain National Park is set separately, and its official rates page could not be read for this article, so budget for that on top if you plan to enter the park on foot elsewhere.

Sources: tablemountain.net, tablemountain.net.

posts.title: Cartagena hotel tax 2026: foreign non residents are billed IVA at 0 percent, not 19
posts.summary: Colombia's DIAN says qualifying tourism services sold to non residents are invoiced with IVA at zero percent, against a general rate of 19 percent. Five nights at 600,000 pesos saves 570,000 pesos.
posts.body:
A foreign non resident staying in a Cartagena hotel should be billed IVA at 0 percent in 2026 rather than the general rate of 19 percent. Colombia's tax authority, the DIAN, states in its published doctrine that qualifying tourism services are invoiced applying IVA at a rate of zero percent, and a separate DIAN ruling records that article 468 of the tax code sets a general rate of 19 percent for the tax.

What you have to show

The DIAN concept sets out the proof. The guest presents an original passport and evidence of entering Colombia without the intention of settling there, and travellers admitted through the automated migration gates may need a migratory movement certificate. The hotel must be registered in the national tourism register, and the exemption rests on article 481 of the tax code, which covers tourism services supplied to people resident abroad. Separately, the trade ministry puts the parafiscal tourism contribution at 2.5 per thousand of an operator's operating income, which is a cost to the business rather than a line on your bill.

A worked example

Five nights in a Cartagena hotel at 600,000 pesos a night is 3,000,000 pesos of room charges. A resident guest would see 570,000 pesos of IVA added, for 3,570,000 in total. A qualifying foreign guest sees 0 pesos of IVA and pays 3,000,000. The saving on that single booking is 570,000 pesos.

What is still unclear

The DIAN documents consulted here do not say what a guest should do if a property charges the tax anyway, so it is worth confirming the zero rate when booking rather than at check out.

Sources: normograma.dian.gov.co, normograma.dian.gov.co, mincit.gov.co.

posts.title: Casablanca taxe de sejour 2026: 25 dirhams per person per night in a five star hotel
posts.summary: Casablanca sets its taxe de sejour by hotel category, from 4 dirhams in a pension to 30 dirhams in the special class, with 25 dirhams per person per night in a five star hotel.
posts.body:
Casablanca charges a taxe de sejour of 25 dirhams per person per night in a five star hotel and 10 dirhams in a four star hotel, according to the tariff list published by the commune of Casablanca on its official city site.

What the commune publishes

The same list sets 7 dirhams for three star hotels and 5 dirhams for two star and one star hotels. Guest houses, congress venues and hotels in the special class are the dearest at 30 dirhams. Private clubs are 25 dirhams, tourist stations 7 dirhams, summer resorts 5 dirhams, and pensions, inns and holiday rentals 4 dirhams. The charge is per person and per night, so it scales with the size of the group rather than with the room.

What a stay costs in 2026

Two people spending four nights in a four star hotel owe 10 dirhams each per night, which is 80 dirhams for the stay. The same pair in a five star hotel owe 200 dirhams across four nights. In a pension the figure falls to 32 dirhams. The hotel collects it and pays the commune every quarter, before the end of the first month following each quarter, so it reaches you as a line on the bill rather than a separate payment.

What is still unclear

The commune page lists the rates and the payment calendar but does not state on that page whether children are exempt, so the age rules are worth confirming when you book.

Sources: casablancacity.ma, casablancacity.ma.

posts.title: Chiang Mai park fees 2026: 300 baht per foreign adult at Doi Inthanon
posts.summary: The Thai national parks department charges foreign adults 300 baht and foreign children 150 baht at Doi Inthanon, the main mountain day trip from Chiang Mai.
posts.body:
A foreign adult pays 300 baht to enter Doi Inthanon National Park, the mountain day trip most Chiang Mai visitors take, and a foreign child pays 150 baht, under the fee schedule attached to the 2564 regulation of the Department of National Parks, Wildlife and Plant Conservation.

How the fee is set

The department does not price parks one by one. It sorts them into four groups and prices the group. Doi Inthanon sits in group 3 alongside Kaeng Krachan, Erawan and Huai Nam Dang, where a Thai adult pays 60 baht and a Thai child 30 baht. Group 1 parks are the cheapest, with a foreign child rate of 50 baht, and the island parks in group 4 are the dearest at 500 baht for a foreign adult. The same country therefore charges four different prices for what looks like the same ticket.

What a visit costs in 2026

Two foreign adults visiting Doi Inthanon for a day pay 600 baht in entrance fees before transport or food. Two adults and two children pay 900 baht. If the week also takes in a group 1 park closer to the city, the second gate is much cheaper, so the order of the itinerary changes the total.

What is still unclear

Thailand has repeatedly discussed a 300 baht arrival fee for air passengers, reported by the news outlet Nation Thailand, but no collection date has been set, so it is not a cost a 2026 visitor pays.

Sources: dnp-app.dnp.go.th, nationthailand.com.

posts.title: Copenhagen tourist tax 2026: none, with 25 percent VAT inside the room rate
posts.summary: Copenhagen still has no tourist tax in 2026. The only tax on a hotel night is Danish VAT at 25 percent of the taxable amount, which is 20 percent of the price you see.
posts.body:
Copenhagen levies no tourist tax at all in 2026. What a visitor actually pays on a hotel room is Danish VAT, which the tax authority sets at 25 percent of the taxable amount.

Why there is no city tax

The city has wanted one. A June 2024 item before the Copenhagen city council states that under section 43 of the Danish constitution no tax may be imposed or collected without statutory authority, which means the city cannot introduce a visitor charge by itself. The same paper models what one would look like, at 1 euro per overnight stay in three of its four models, and a version scaled by district at 2.5 euros in the inner city, 1.5 euros in Vesterbro and 0.75 euros further out. None of that is in force.

What a stay costs in 2026

Because VAT at 25 percent of the base equals 20 percent of the price including VAT, a room advertised at 1,500 kroner per night carries 300 kroner of tax. Three nights at that rate is 4,500 kroner, of which 900 kroner is VAT already inside the price rather than added at the desk. Nothing further is charged for being a visitor.

What is still unclear

Whether parliament grants councils the power to charge visitors remains open, so the zero is a snapshot of 2026 rather than a guarantee for later trips.

Sources: kk.dk, info.skat.dk.

posts.title: Cusco tourist ticket 2026: 130 soles for the ten day boleto integral
posts.summary: COSITUC prices the full Cusco tourist ticket at 130 soles for foreign visitors with ten days of validity, and each of the three partial circuits at 70 soles.
posts.body:
The Boleto Turistico del Cusco costs 130 soles for a foreign visitor in 2026, and the body that issues it, COSITUC, gives that ticket ten days of validity.

What the ticket buys

COSITUC publishes one full ticket and three partial ones. The integral ticket at 130 soles covers all three circuits. Each partial ticket costs 70 soles: the Saqsayhuaman circuit, the city circuit and the Sacred Valley circuit. Partial ticket one is valid for a single day, and partial tickets two and three for two days each. A foreign student ticket costs 70 soles and also runs for ten days.

What a trip costs in 2026

Two foreign adults buying the integral ticket spend 260 soles between them before any transport. A couple who only want the Sacred Valley pay 140 soles for two partial tickets and get two days to use them. Because every partial ticket costs the same 70 soles, buying any two of them costs more than the full ticket, which is the arithmetic that pushes most visitors to the integral version even when they only plan on two circuits.

What is still unclear

Machu Picchu is not part of this ticket and is sold separately, and the COSITUC tariff does not carry that price, so budget it as a second line.

Sources: cosituc.gob.pe, cosituc.gob.pe.

posts.title: Dubai Tourism Dirham 2026: 20 dirhams per room per night in a five star hotel
posts.summary: Dubai charges the Tourism Dirham per room per night, from 7 dirhams in a budget hotel to 20 in a five star, capped at thirty consecutive nights.
posts.body:
Dubai charges a Tourism Dirham of 20 dirhams per room per night in a five star hotel, set out in Schedule 1 of Executive Council Resolution No. 2 of 2014 on the emirate legislation portal.

The full schedule

The same schedule sets 15 dirhams for a four star hotel, 10 dirhams for three star and two star hotels, and 7 dirhams for one star and budget hotels. Serviced apartments are priced separately at 20, 15 and 10 dirhams for luxury, deluxe and standard grades, guest houses at 7 dirhams, and holiday homes at 15 or 10 dirhams by grade. The fee is per room, not per guest, so two people sharing pay it once.

What a stay costs in 2026

Five nights in a five star hotel adds 100 dirhams to the room bill. The same five nights in a three star hotel adds 50 dirhams. Long stays are capped: the amending resolution says a guest is charged for a maximum of thirty consecutive nights, so two months in a five star hotel still stops at 600 dirhams.

What is still unclear

Dubai hotel bills often show municipality and service lines as well, and this resolution does not set those, so the Tourism Dirham is only one line of the final total.

Sources: dlp.dubai.gov.ae, dlp.dubai.gov.ae.

posts.title: Dublin tourist tax 2026: none, and 13.5 percent VAT on the room
posts.summary: Dublin charges no visitor levy in 2026. Revenue taxes guest and holiday accommodation at the reduced VAT rate of 13.5 percent, which sits inside the advertised price.
posts.body:
Dublin has no tourist tax in 2026. The only tax on a hotel night is VAT, which Revenue applies to guest and holiday accommodation at the reduced rate of 13.5 percent.

What Revenue says

Revenue states that a supply of guest or holiday accommodation is taxable at the reduced rate of Value Added Tax, and that the duration of the stay does not affect the treatment. Its rate table effective from 1 January 2026 puts the standard rate at 23 percent, the reduced rate at 13.5 percent and the second reduced rate at 9 percent. From 1 July 2026 restaurant and catering moved to the 9 percent band, but the room itself stays at 13.5 percent.

What a stay costs in 2026

VAT here sits inside the advertised price rather than being added at checkout. A room priced at 200 euros per night therefore contains about 23.79 euros of VAT, and three nights at that price contains about 71.36 euros. Nothing extra is charged for being a visitor, and no city collects a bed tax.

What is still unclear

A city levy keeps being proposed. RTE reported in June 2026 that the government would not oppose councils collecting a tourist tax, but enabling legislation would still be needed first, so the answer for a 2026 trip is nil.

Sources: revenue.ie, revenue.ie, rte.ie.

posts.title: Dubrovnik tourist tax 2026: 2.65 euros per person per night in season
posts.summary: The county decision on the 2026 tourist tax sets Dubrovnik at 2.65 euros per person per night from 1 April to 30 September and 1.85 euros the rest of the year.
posts.body:
Dubrovnik charges a tourist tax of 2.65 euros per person per night between 1 April and 30 September 2026, and 1.85 euros per person per night for the rest of the year, under the decision on the amount of the tourist tax adopted by the county assembly.

How the county sets it

The decision covers every town and municipality in the county in one table, and Dubrovnik carries the highest nightly rate of any of them. Campsites in the city area are cheaper, at 1.95 euros in season and 1.30 euros outside it. Owners of holiday homes pay an annual lump sum instead, at 33 euros for the first family member, 33 euros for the second and 13 euros for each further one.

What a stay costs in 2026

Two adults spending five nights in a Dubrovnik hotel in July owe 26.50 euros in tourist tax on top of the room. The same stay in November costs 18.50 euros. A week in August for a family of four comes to 74.20 euros if everyone is charged the adult rate. It is collected by the property and usually appears on the final bill rather than in the booking price.

What is still unclear

The county decision lists amounts and not exemptions, so any reduction for children comes from the national law on the tourist tax rather than from this document.

Sources: dnz.hr.

posts.title: Ho Chi Minh City 2026: 25 US dollars for a single entry Vietnam electronic visa
posts.summary: Circular 28 of 2026 from the Ministry of Finance prices Vietnam's electronic visa at 25 US dollars for single entry and 50 for multiple entry, effective 1 April 2026.
posts.body:
Vietnam charges 25 US dollars for a single entry electronic visa, the document most visitors to Ho Chi Minh City arrive on, under circular 28 of 2026 from the Ministry of Finance, which the government news portal reports took effect on 1 April 2026.

The fee schedule

The circular prices a single entry electronic visa at 25 dollars and a multiple entry electronic visa at 50 dollars where the validity runs up to 90 days. Longer multiple entry categories climb from there, reaching 165 dollars for the band covering five to ten years. The fee is set nationally by the finance ministry, so it does not vary by which airport you land at.

What a trip costs in 2026

Two travellers flying into Ho Chi Minh City on single entry electronic visas pay 50 dollars between them before anything else in the budget. A couple planning a side trip to Cambodia and a return need the multiple entry version, which doubles the pair to 100 dollars. Against a week of accommodation the visa is small, but it is charged per person and paid before departure.

What is still unclear

The fee is national and no separate Ho Chi Minh City accommodation levy appears in the official schedule, so a city tax of the European kind is not something we could find published for the city.

Sources: baochinhphu.vn.

posts.title: Hoi An ancient town ticket 2026: 120,000 dong for foreign visitors
posts.summary: The Hoi An old town entrance ticket is 120,000 dong for international visitors and 80,000 dong for domestic visitors, per the Vietnamese government news portal.
posts.body:
The Hoi An ancient town ticket costs 120,000 dong for an international visitor and 80,000 dong for a domestic visitor, the prices the Vietnamese government news portal quoted when the town began enforcing the ticket at every entrance to the protected area.

What the ticket is

This is not a city tax. It is an entrance ticket to the protected old town, and the announcement said the receipts go to conserving and restoring the monuments, along with cultural programming, tourism infrastructure, sanitation and security. The same announcement recorded the price as unchanged since 2012, which makes it one of the more stable numbers in Vietnamese tourism.

What a visit costs in 2026

Two international visitors pay 240,000 dong to walk into the old town and a group of four pays 480,000 dong. Set against a night in a Hoi An hotel the ticket is a modest line, but it is charged per person rather than per booking, so it grows with the group and it is separate from anything you spend inside.

What is still unclear

The clearest official statement of the price is the 2023 government announcement and we found no newer figure published on a government page, so confirm the current rate at the ticket booth.

Sources: baochinhphu.vn.

posts.title: Hong Kong hotel accommodation tax 2026: 3 percent on the room charge
posts.summary: Hong Kong's Inland Revenue Department applies a 3 percent hotel accommodation tax on room charges, in force since 1 January 2025, with three narrow exemptions.
posts.body:
Hong Kong charges a hotel accommodation tax of 3 percent on the room charge. The Inland Revenue Department states that with effect from 1 January 2025 the rate was adjusted from 0 percent to 3 percent, and that is the rate the department publishes for 2026.

What the tax covers

It applies to accommodation charges received by hotels or guesthouses, which the department defines as the sum payable by or on behalf of guests for accommodation received. Three exemptions are listed: a daily accommodation charge of less than 15 dollars, accommodation provided by a society not established or conducted for profit, and a hotel containing less than 10 rooms normally available for lodging guests.

What a stay costs in 2026

A room at 1,200 Hong Kong dollars per night carries 36 dollars of tax, so four nights adds 144 dollars. At 2,500 dollars per night the same four nights adds 300 dollars. Because it is a percentage rather than a flat nightly charge, it scales with the room, and it lands on the accommodation element rather than on meals or services billed separately.

What is still unclear

Hotels differ in whether they show the 3 percent as its own line beside a service charge or fold it into the headline rate, and the department page does not govern how a hotel presents it.

Sources: ird.gov.hk, ird.gov.hk.

posts.title: Istanbul accommodation tax 2026: 1 percent until 31 December
posts.summary: Turkey's accommodation tax was redetermined at 1 percent until 31 December 2026 by presidential decision 11263, published in the official gazette on 1 May 2026.
posts.body:
The accommodation tax on a hotel night in Istanbul is 1 percent in 2026. The explanatory note published by the Turkish Revenue Administration on presidential decision 11263 says the rate in the fifth paragraph of article 34 of law 6802 was redetermined as 1 percent until 31 December 2026, that date included.

How the cut happened

The decision is dated 30 April 2026 and was published in the official gazette, issue 33240, on 1 May 2026. The note gives the legal basis and the end date. It does not set out the mechanics of collection, which sit in the general communique on the accommodation tax published separately by the same administration.

What a stay costs in 2026

A room at 4,000 lira per night carries 40 lira of accommodation tax, so three nights adds 120 lira. A suite at 10,000 lira a night adds 100 lira per night. Because the tax is a percentage and not a flat nightly charge, it scales with what you book, and on a normal Istanbul city break it is a minor line rather than a real cost.

What is still unclear

The reduction is written to expire on 31 December 2026 and the note says nothing about what applies from 1 January 2027, so a stay booked into next year may not be taxed at 1 percent.

Sources: cdn.gib.gov.tr.

posts.title: Jaipur monument entry fees 2026: 500 rupees for a foreign adult at Amber Fort
posts.summary: Rajasthan's official booking portal prices Amber Fort at 500 rupees for foreign adults in 2026, with Hawa Mahal, Jantar Mantar and Nahargarh at 200 rupees each.
posts.body:
A foreign adult pays 500 rupees to enter Amber Fort in 2026, against 100 rupees for an Indian adult, according to the Rajasthan government official booking portal for state monuments. Jaipur levies no per night bed tax on visitors, so monument tickets are the charge the state sets on tourists most directly.

What each site costs

The same portal lists a general ticket of 200 rupees for foreign adults at Hawa Mahal, Jantar Mantar and Nahargarh Fort, with Indian adults at 50 rupees and students paying less on production of a valid identity card. Entry is free for children below 7 years, and free for everyone on four listed days including World Heritage Day on 18 April and World Tourism Day on 27 September.

The composite ticket maths

The composite ticket is 1,000 rupees for a foreign adult and 400 rupees for an Indian adult. Buying separate tickets for Amber Fort, Hawa Mahal, Jantar Mantar and Nahargarh comes to 1,100 rupees for one foreign adult in 2026, so the composite is already 100 rupees cheaper across those four. Two foreign adults doing the same circuit pay 2,000 rupees on composite tickets rather than 2,200.

What is still unclear

The portal pages read here do not state how long the composite ticket remains valid or the full list of monuments it admits you to, so the saving above is only proven for the four sites priced above.

Sources: Rajasthan official booking portal, Amber Fort and the same portal for Hawa Mahal.

posts.title: Kathmandu tourist visa fee 2026: 30 US dollars for 15 days, 50 for 30 days
posts.summary: Nepal charges 30 US dollars for a 15 day tourist visa, 50 for 30 days and 125 for 90 days in 2026, all multiple entry, per the Nepal Tourism Board fee list.
posts.body:
A tourist visa for Nepal costs 30 US dollars for 15 days, 50 dollars for 30 days and 125 dollars for 90 days in 2026, and all three are multiple entry, according to the fee list published by the Nepal Tourism Board. Kathmandu itself publishes no nightly bed tax alongside it, so the visa is the fixed government charge most visitors meet first.

Who pays nothing

The tourism board lists gratis visas for children below 10 years except United States citizens, and for citizens of SAARC countries other than Afghanistan for up to 30 days on a first visit in a given visa year. Non Resident Nepali cardholders and Chinese nationals are also listed as free.

A worked example

Two adults trekking for three weeks each need the 30 day visa, so 100 dollars for the pair in 2026. Add a child of 8 on a non United States passport and the total does not move, because that child is gratis. A couple staying 12 days pays 60 dollars instead, by taking the 15 day visa rather than rounding up to 30 days.

What is still unclear

The board list gives the fee in dollars or equivalent convertible currency but does not say what payment methods the airport accepts in 2026, and it does not cover the separate trekking permits and national park fees charged outside the city.

Sources: Nepal Tourism Board, tourist visa.

posts.title: Krakow tourist tax 2026: zero per night, against a Polish ceiling of 3.46 zloty
posts.summary: Krakow charges no tourist tax per night in 2026. Poland caps the local fee at 3.46 zloty per day, and Krakow lost the right to levy it in 2015.
posts.body:
Krakow charges nothing per night in tourist tax in 2026. The city convention bureau, on the municipal site, states that Krakow collected a local fee between 2004 and 2015 and that it was abolished following changes in environmental protection regulations, because the city and its metropolitan area no longer met the required criteria.

What Polish law allows

The fee Krakow lost is the oplata miejscowa, which only municipalities meeting climate related criteria may levy. The Ministry of Finance notice of 1 August 2025, published in Monitor Polski, sets the ceilings for 2026 at 3.46 zloty per day for the local fee, 4.89 zloty per day in spa protection areas and 6.67 zloty for the spa fee itself.

What a stay costs

Four nights in Krakow for two people in 2026 adds zero zloty of accommodation tax to the bill. Had the city been allowed to charge the national maximum, those 8 person nights would have cost 27.68 zloty, which is roughly one museum ticket. That is the size of the sum being argued about.

What is still unclear

The city is lobbying the government to let any municipality introduce a tourist fee. No date for such a law is published, so the zero holds for now but is not guaranteed for the whole of 2026.

Sources: Krakow Convention Bureau on the tourist tax and Monitor Polski, maximum local tax rates for 2026.

posts.title: Las Vegas room tax 2026: 13.38 percent in the gaming corridor, 13 percent outside
posts.summary: City of Las Vegas room tax instructions revised in March 2026 set 13.38 percent inside the Primary Gaming Corridor and 13.00 percent outside it.
posts.body:
A Las Vegas hotel bill carries room tax of 13.38 percent inside the Primary Gaming Corridor and 13.00 percent outside it in 2026, according to the room tax instructions issued by the City of Las Vegas Business License Division and revised in March 2026.

How it is charged

The same document says the licensee or operator is responsible for collecting and remitting the tax, and that it must be shown to the guest as a separate charge rather than folded into the room price. If an operator fails to collect it, the city still takes the tax out of the operator own funds, and anything over collected has to be remitted as well.

A worked example

Three nights at 220 dollars a night is 660 dollars of room revenue. At 13.38 percent the tax is 88.31 dollars, taking the room line to 748.31 dollars before any resort fee. The same booking a short distance outside the corridor is taxed at 13.00 percent, or 85.80 dollars, a difference of 2.51 dollars across the stay.

What is still unclear

Whether a property sits inside the Primary Gaming Corridor is decided by a map in the city appendix rather than by street address, and the city tells operators to confirm their own rate by phone, so a guest cannot verify the 0.38 point difference from a booking page.

Sources: City of Las Vegas room tax instructions and guidelines.

posts.title: Lima hotel tax 2026: 0 percent IGV for foreign visitors instead of 18 percent
posts.summary: Peru treats hotel stays by non domiciled visitors as an export for up to 60 days per entry, so the 18 percent IGV should not appear on a Lima hotel bill in 2026.
posts.body:
A foreign visitor staying in a Lima hotel in 2026 should be billed 0 percent IGV rather than the standard 18 percent. Peru IGV law, in the text published by the tax authority SUNAT, treats accommodation supplied to non domiciled guests as an export, and SUNAT guidance for taxpayers states that the rate applicable to a taxable operation is 18 percent.

The 60 day rule

The law counts hotel services, including food, supplied to non domiciled persons individually or through a tour package as an export for the period of their stay, up to 60 days per entry into the country. Past that point the relief stops. The hotel has to see a passport or an equivalent travel document valid for entry before applying it.

A worked example

Five nights at 300 soles a night is 1,500 soles. With IGV at 18 percent a domestic guest pays 1,770 soles, while a qualifying foreign guest pays 1,500 soles, a difference of 270 soles on one short stay. Lima adds no separate city bed tax on top of that.

What is still unclear

The relief only helps if the hotel operates it. The law leaves the registration, records and procedures to a separate regulation, so smaller Lima properties may still show 18 percent on the invoice in 2026.

Sources: SUNAT, IGV law chapter on exports and SUNAT guidance on the IGV rate.

posts.title: Lisbon tourist tax 2026: 4 euros per person per night
posts.summary: Lisbon municipal tourist tax on overnight stays is 4 euros per person per night in 2026, a figure set by the city notice published in its own municipal bulletin.
posts.body:
Lisbon municipal tourist tax is 4 euros per person per night in 2026. The figure comes from the city own Boletim Municipal, where edital 234/2024 records the change to the regulation that carried the unit value to 4 euros per overnight stay, in force from 1 September 2024.

Who collects it

That notice states the change was published in the Diario da Republica of 26 August 2024 and points anyone in doubt to the city finance department, which runs the tax. The charge falls on the guest and is handed over by the accommodation operator, which is why it appears as its own line at checkout rather than inside the advertised room rate.

A worked example

Two adults staying five nights in Lisbon in 2026 pay 40 euros in tourist tax, on top of the room price and Portuguese VAT. One traveller on a three night city break pays 12 euros. On a cheap hostel bed the tax can be a tenth of the nightly price, while on a five star room it disappears into the rounding.

What is still unclear

The notice sets only the unit value. Any cap on how many nights of a single stay are taxed, and the age below which a guest is exempt, sit in the wider municipal regulation rather than in the notice that fixed the 4 euro figure, so both are worth checking on the operator invoice.

Sources: informacoeseservicos.lisboa.pt, Camara Municipal de Lisboa, Boletim Municipal 1593, edital 234/2024.

posts.title: London tourist tax 2026: no overnight levy, and a 20 pound ETA
posts.summary: England has no overnight visitor levy in 2026; the government is only consulting on the power. The fixed charge for most visitors is the 20 pound ETA.
posts.body:
London charges no overnight visitor levy in 2026. The UK government consultation on an overnight visitor levy in England describes it as giving Mayoral Strategic Authorities in England the power to create local overnight visitor levies, which is a power still being designed rather than a charge already on hotel bills.

What visitors do pay

The fixed government charge is the Electronic Travel Authorisation. Gov.uk states that an ETA costs 20 pounds and lets the holder travel to the UK, Jersey, Guernsey or the Isle of Man for up to 6 months. Hotel rooms carry standard VAT, which is already inside the advertised price rather than added at the desk.

A worked example

Two adults on a four night London trip in 2026 pay 40 pounds between them for ETAs and nothing per night to the city. In a European capital charging 4 euros per person per night, the same four nights would have added 32 euros of city tax on top of the room.

What is still unclear

The consultation ran from 26 November 2025 to 18 February 2026. Whether the Mayor of London eventually sets a levy, at what rate, and from what date, is open.

Sources: UK government consultation on an overnight visitor levy in England and gov.uk on the Electronic Travel Authorisation.

posts.title: Maldives green tax 2026: 12 US dollars per night at resorts, 6 at small guesthouses
posts.summary: The Maldives green tax is 12 US dollars per tourist per day at resorts and 6 dollars at guesthouses of 50 rooms or fewer on inhabited islands, plus 17 percent TGST.
posts.body:
The Maldives green tax is 12 US dollars per tourist per day at resorts and most hotels in 2026, and 6 dollars per day at a guesthouse or hotel on an inhabited island with 50 or fewer registered rooms. The Ministry of Finance sets it out in exactly those terms, dates the current rates to 1 January 2025 and records that children under the age of 2 years are exempt.

What else lands on the bill

The same ministry page gives the Tourism Goods and Services Tax as 17 percent, against 8 percent for general goods and services. Green tax receipts go to the Maldives Green Fund, a trust fund earmarked for climate mitigation and other environmental work rather than the general budget.

A worked example

Two adults on a seven night resort stay owe 14 person nights of green tax at 12 dollars, which is 168 dollars, before anything else. The same couple in a small guesthouse pays 84 dollars. On a 3,000 dollar room bill, TGST at 17 percent adds a further 510 dollars, so tax alone on the resort trip is 678 dollars.

What is still unclear

The ministry credits the current rates to the thirteenth amendment to the Tourism Act while also listing a fourteenth amendment, so the amendment numbering behind the 12 dollar figure is worth checking with the tax authority before quoting it.

Sources: Maldives Ministry of Finance, revenue policy.

posts.title: Manila departure tax 2026: 1,620 pesos economy Philippine travel tax
