What is not stated on that page is whether the separate exhibition spaces inside the compound are included in the adult ticket or charged again.

Sources: dinhdoclap.gov.vn.

posts.title: My Son Sanctuary tickets 2026: 150,000 dong for foreign visitors
posts.summary: Foreign visitors pay 150,000 dong at My Son in 2026 and Vietnamese visitors 100,000, with a 30,000 dong service ticket for children aged 5 to 15.
posts.body:
A foreign visitor ticket to the My Son Sanctuary, the Cham temple complex inland from Hoi An, costs 150,000 dong in 2026, according to the official My Son ticketing site. Vietnamese visitors pay 100,000 dong for the same entry. Both figures are described on that page as final prices with tax already included, so there is no surcharge at the gate.

The third line on the price table

There is a service ticket at 30,000 dong. The site explains that children under 5 enter free and that children aged 5 to 15 buy the service ticket, which covers transport inside the site rather than admission. The electric shuttle between the entrance and the temple groups is the part that money buys.

Hours

The ticket office sells from 6am to 5:30pm and the site itself is open from 6am to 6pm. Arriving after 5:30pm means no ticket at all, whatever the gate looks like, and the gap between the two closing times is the most expensive half hour of the day to get wrong.

A worked example

Two foreign adults with two children aged 5 to 15 pay 300,000 dong for the adult tickets plus 60,000 dong in service tickets, so 360,000 dong before any transport from Hoi An. A couple with no children pays 300,000 dong. What the site does not make clear in English is whether adults are also expected to buy the 30,000 dong service ticket, or whether the shuttle is already covered by the higher foreign rate.

Sources: mysonticketonline.vn.

posts.title: Ngong Ping 360 tickets 2026: 295 dollars for a standard round trip
posts.summary: A standard cabin round trip on the Ngong Ping 360 cable car is 295 Hong Kong dollars for an adult in 2026 and 150 for a child aged 3 to 11.
posts.body:
A standard cabin round trip on the Ngong Ping 360 cable car costs 295 Hong Kong dollars for an adult in 2026, according to the operator's own cable car ticket page. Children aged 3 to 11 pay 150 dollars, and infants aged 0 to 2 travel free.

Glass floor cabins cost more

The Crystal Cabin, the one with the glass floor, is 365 dollars for an adult round trip and 220 for a child. Crystal Plus is 545 adult and 400 child. A combo of one Crystal leg and one standard leg is 330 adult and 185 child, which is the cheapest way to try the glass floor once rather than twice.

The senior rate is not for visitors

The page prices a senior standard round trip at 155 dollars, but states that the senior fare applies only to Hong Kong residents holding a valid JoyYou card. A visiting grandparent pays the full 295. The same page shows no difference between booking online and paying at the ticket office, so the saving people expect from advance booking is not published.

A worked example

Two adults and two children aged 3 to 11 on standard round trips pay 890 Hong Kong dollars. The same family in Crystal Cabins pays 1,170. Upgrading only one leg through the combo ticket brings that to 1,030. What the page does not show is a single trip price, so anyone planning to walk one way should confirm that at the counter.

Sources: np360.com.hk.

posts.title: Hagia Sophia tickets 2026: 25 euros for foreign visitors
posts.summary: Foreign visitors pay 25 euros at Hagia Sophia in 2026, priced in euros rather than lira, with midday Friday and early morning closures to plan around.
posts.body:
Foreign visitors to Hagia Sophia pay 25 euros in 2026, according to the Turkish culture ministry's own museum page for the building. The price is quoted in euros rather than lira, which means it does not drift with the exchange rate the way most Turkish museum prices do.

What the ticket covers

The ministry page says the ticket lets you see the sanctuary floor of the mosque and the Ottoman period annexes, pass through the Marble Door, and examine the Byzantine period mosaics. It also includes an augmented reality experience delivered through mobile headsets in 23 languages, which is bundled rather than sold separately.

Hours and the closures that catch people

The page gives opening hours of 9am to 7:30pm every day, labelling those as the 2025 hours. Two closures matter more than the price. The visiting area shuts between 12 and 2 on Fridays for Friday prayers, and the praying area is closed to visitors from the morning prayer until 10am each day for cleaning and maintenance. A Friday lunchtime slot is the single worst arrival time in the week.

A worked example

A couple pays 50 euros. A family of two adults and two teenagers pays 100 euros, because the ministry page publishes no child, student or senior reduction against the 25 euro foreign visitor rate. What is not clear from that page is whether the hours it labels 2025 carry into 2026 unchanged.

Sources: muze.gen.tr.

posts.title: City Palace Jaipur tickets 2026: 400 rupees for the museum
posts.summary: The City Palace Museum in Jaipur charges 400 rupees adult in 2026, 200 reduced, and 500 for the composite ticket, according to its own admission page.
posts.body:
Entry to the City Palace Museum in Jaipur is 400 rupees for an adult in 2026, according to the palace's own admission page. Students, young visitors and children under 12 pay 200 rupees, and the same 200 rupee rate covers senior citizens and defence personnel.

The composite ticket

The composite ticket is 500 rupees adult and 300 rupees reduced, adding more of the complex than the museum ticket alone. The gap over the basic ticket is only 100 rupees, which makes the museum only version rarely the better buy. At the top end, the Chandra Mahal Royal Tour is 4,000 rupees adult and 2,000 reduced, and the small Jaipur Centre for Art is 100 rupees.

Timing and closures

The museum runs 9:30am to 6:30pm seven days a week, with the last tickets sold at 6pm. The page flags that the Museum at Night slot, priced at 510 rupees adult, is temporarily closed, and that the Textile Gallery closes from 27 March 2026 for restoration. The palace also closes on Dhulandi, the second day of Holi, which is the one date in the year to avoid outright.

A worked example

Two adults and one child under 12 on composite tickets pay 1,300 rupees. The same three on museum only tickets pay 1,000 rupees. The rates published on that page are the Indian national and resident rates, and it shows no separate foreign visitor tariff, which is the figure most overseas visitors actually need before they arrive.

Sources: citypalace.org.

posts.title: Schindler's Factory tickets 2026: 60 zloty for a normal ticket
posts.summary: Oskar Schindler's Enamel Factory in Krakow charges 60 zloty normal, 45 reduced and 120 for a family of four in 2026, with free Mondays that cannot be booked.
posts.body:
A normal ticket to Oskar Schindler's Enamel Factory in Krakow costs 60 zloty in 2026, according to the Museum of Krakow's own page for the branch. A reduced ticket is 45 zloty, and a family ticket covering a maximum of four people is 120 zloty.

Guided tours cost half as much again

The museum prices a regular tour in English at 90 zloty normal and 75 zloty reduced. Groups pay 45 zloty a head, and school groups 26 zloty a head, so a small private group is charged the reduced rate rather than a premium.

The booking rules

Tickets go on sale 90 days before the visit date, online sales close 6 hours before the visit, and there is a limit of 5 tickets per person in one purchase. Monday is the free admission day, and the museum states that on free admission days it is impossible to book tickets in advance, which turns the free day into a queueing exercise. The branch opens 10am to 3pm on Monday and 9am to 8pm from Tuesday to Sunday, closes on the first Tuesday of the month, and stops admitting visitors 90 minutes before closing.

A worked example

Two adults and two children pay 120 zloty on the family ticket, against 210 zloty if the adults paid full price and the children reduced, so the family ticket is the obvious choice for any qualifying group of four. Two adults on the English guided tour pay 180 zloty. The page does not state the age limits behind the reduced ticket, which is the first thing a family should check.

Sources: muzeumkrakowa.pl.

posts.title: Dubai Safari Park tickets 2026: 50 dirhams for the park pass
posts.summary: The Dubai Safari Park Pass is 50 dirhams in 2026 and covers every zone, the train and the shows, but the park is shut for the season until October 2026.
posts.body:
The Dubai Safari Park Pass costs 50 dirhams in 2026, according to the park's own website, and it covers entry to all zones, unlimited train rides, the Arabian Desert Safari, the shows and the workshops. Children under 3 enter free, as do people of determination with one companion.

The season is the catch

The park closes over the hottest months. Its own site currently shows it closed for the season, with season 8 due to reopen in October 2026. Winter hours, from November to March, are 9am to 8pm, and summer hours, from April to October, are 9am to 6pm, with last entry an hour before closing. Anyone planning a Dubai trip in the summer should treat the park as unavailable rather than assume a reduced schedule.

Upgrades

The Safari Bundle at 117 dirhams, sold online only, adds a 35 minute Explorer Safari tour to the standard pass. The private experiences are priced by group rather than per person: a behind the scenes tour is 1,450 dirhams for up to 10 people over 90 minutes, the King of Safari VIP experience is 2,500 dirhams for up to 10 people over 4 hours, and breakfast with giraffes or lions is 2,150 dirhams for up to 6 people.

A worked example

Two adults and two children over 3 pay 200 dirhams on the standard pass. The same family on the online only Safari Bundle pays 468 dirhams. The site publishes no separate adult and child price for the basic pass, so 50 dirhams appears to apply to everyone aged 3 and over, which is the one point worth confirming at the gate.

Sources: dubaisafari.ae.

posts.title: Nijo Castle tickets 2026: 1,300 yen for castle and palace
posts.summary: Nijo Castle in Kyoto charges 1,300 yen in 2026 for the grounds plus Ninomaru Palace, or 800 yen for the grounds alone, according to the castle's own fee page.
posts.body:
Nijo Castle charges 1,300 yen in 2026 for the combined ticket covering the castle grounds and Ninomaru Palace, according to the fee page published by the castle itself. The grounds only ticket is 800 yen. On that same page, junior high and high school students pay 400 yen and elementary school students pay 300 yen for castle admission.

The third ticket most visitors miss

Honmaru Palace is sold separately and is not covered by either ticket above. The castle's fee page lists it at 1,000 yen for adults, 300 yen for junior and senior high school students and 200 yen for elementary school students, states that advance reservations are required, and adds that a castle admission ticket is still needed on top. Group rates do not apply there, which the page attributes to protection of cultural properties.

Days that quietly cost money

The castle site gives entry from 8:45 in the morning with last admission at 4:00 and closing at 5:00. The whole site closes 29 to 31 December. Ninomaru Palace closes 26 to 28 December and 1 to 3 January plus selected Tuesdays. Honmaru Palace closes the third Monday of every month and the day after.

What a couple pays

Two adults on the combined castle and Ninomaru ticket pay 2,600 yen. Adding Honmaru Palace for both takes it to 4,600 yen, and that second part has to be reserved before arrival rather than bought at the gate.

The fee page does not spell out whether student rates apply to the combined ticket or only to plain castle admission, so a family should budget the adult figure if unsure.

Sources: nijo-jocastle.city.kyoto.lg.jp, nijo-jocastle.city.kyoto.lg.jp, nijo-jocastle.city.kyoto.lg.jp.

posts.title: Neon Museum tickets 2026: 25 dollars by day, 35 at night
posts.summary: The Neon Museum in Las Vegas lists adult daytime admission at 25 dollars in 2026 and evening admission at 35 dollars, with concessions at 20 and 30, on its own admission pages.
posts.body:
The Neon Museum charges 25 dollars for an adult daytime ticket in 2026 and 35 dollars for an adult evening ticket, according to the museum's own admission pages. Seniors aged 65 and over with identification, students with identification, military with identification and Nevada residents with identification all pay 20 dollars by day and 30 dollars in the evening. Children aged 7 to 17 pay 12.50 by day and 17.50 at night.

Day and night are two different products

The museum sells daytime and evening admission as separate listings rather than one ticket with a time slot, and the ten dollar gap between them is the single biggest variable in the price. Under 6s are admitted free, but the daytime page is explicit that a ticket is still required for them, so they have to be added to the booking rather than simply walked in.

The fee that is not in the headline

The daytime page notes that a ticket processing fee applies. That fee sits on top of every figure above, so the checkout total will always be higher than the advertised number. The museum also publishes a Nevada resident rate at the same level as the senior and student rate, which is worth knowing if anyone in the party has state identification.

What a family pays

Two adults and two teenagers aged 7 to 17 pay 25 plus 25 plus 12.50 plus 12.50, which is 75 dollars by day before the processing fee. The same four at night pay 105 dollars.

The museum does not publish the size of the ticket processing fee on the admission pages, so the true online total cannot be worked out from official sources alone.

posts.title: Museo Larco tickets 2026: 50 soles general admission
posts.summary: Museo Larco in Lima lists general admission at 50 soles for 2026, 35 for over 60s, 25 for students and minors and 1 sol for children aged 3 to 8, on its own visit page.
posts.body:
Museo Larco charges 50 soles for general admission in 2026, according to the museum's own visit page. Visitors over 60 pay 35 soles. Students and minors aged 9 to 17 pay 25 soles. Children aged 3 to 8 pay 1 sol, and children aged 0 to 2 are free. That spread means the difference between a well documented family group and a badly documented one is real money at the desk.

Opening days are the easy part

The same page gives opening as Monday to Sunday, 9:00 in the morning to 7:00 in the evening, which is unusually generous for a Lima museum and removes the closed on Monday trap that catches people elsewhere in the city. The exceptions are 24, 25 and 26 December and 1 January, when the museum closes at 6:00 in the evening instead. There is no published gate versus online split, so the price is the price whichever way you buy.

What a family actually pays

Two adults, one child of 10 and one child of 6 pay 50 plus 50 plus 25 plus 1, which is 126 soles. Two adults alone pay 100 soles. A couple over 60 pay 70 soles. Because the 3 to 8 rate is a single sol, a family with young children pays barely more than the two adults would on their own, which is the opposite of how most museum pricing works.

The museum's page does not state whether the student rate needs a Peruvian student card or accepts any valid card, so foreign students should carry documentation and expect the general rate if it is refused.

Sources: museolarco.org, museolarco.org, museolarco.org.

posts.title: Oceanario de Lisboa tickets 2026: 25 to 29 euros by time slot
posts.summary: Oceanario de Lisboa prices adult entry at 29 euros in the morning, 27 in the early afternoon and 25 in the late afternoon for 2026, with 5 percent off online, per its own ticket page.
posts.body:
Oceanario de Lisboa charges between 25 and 29 euros for an adult ticket in 2026 depending on when you go in, according to the aquarium's own ticket page. The morning slot from 10:00 to 11:30 is 29 euros, the early afternoon slot from 12:00 to 15:30 is 27 euros, and the late afternoon slot from 16:00 to 18:30 is 25 euros. The page summarises this as tickets from 25 euros, which is the cheapest slot rather than the usual price.

Children and seniors follow the same curve

Children aged 3 to 12 pay 17, 16 or 15 euros across the same three slots. Visitors aged 65 and over pay 19, 18 or 17 euros. Children aged 0 to 2 are free. There is also a flexiticket at 41 euros per adult with no fixed date or time, valid for one visit within seven days, which costs about 12 euros more than simply booking the cheapest slot.

The online discount and the clock

The ticket page advertises 5 percent off when buying online with the code ONLINE5, so the gate price is effectively the higher one. Opening is daily 10:00 to 20:00 with last entry at 19:00, which means the late afternoon slot is the last one sold and the one most likely to be gone on a busy day.

What a family pays

Two adults and two children aged 3 to 12 in the late afternoon slot pay 25 plus 25 plus 15 plus 15, which is 80 euros, or about 76 euros after the online discount. The same four in the morning slot pay 92 euros. Choosing the time of day is worth roughly 12 euros to that family.

The page does not say whether the 5 percent code applies to the flexiticket as well as the timed slots.

Sources: oceanario.pt, oceanario.pt, oceanario.pt.

posts.title: Westminster Abbey tickets 2026: 31 pounds for adults
posts.summary: Westminster Abbey lists adult entry at 31 pounds for 2026, with 28 for over 65s and students and 14 for children aged 6 to 17, plus a temporary summer reduction, on its own prices page.
posts.body:
Westminster Abbey charges 31 pounds for an adult ticket in 2026, according to the Abbey's own prices and entry times page. Visitors aged 65 and over pay 28 pounds and students pay 28 pounds. Children aged 6 to 17 pay 14 pounds and children aged 0 to 5 are free. The page also lists a family rate of one adult plus one child at 31 pounds.

The summer discount was temporary

For visits between 25 June and 1 September 2026 the Abbey published lower prices under a UK government campaign, showing 27.13 for adults, 24.50 for over 65s and students and 12.25 for children aged 6 to 17. The page states that savings apply to full price entry tickets only and that anyone who had already bought at the full rate for that window was eligible for a refund down to the discounted rate. Outside that window the prices revert to the 31 pound level.

Closures are the real risk

General admission runs roughly 9:30 in the morning to 3:30 in the afternoon, with hours that vary by date. More importantly, the Abbey warns that it is a working church and is sometimes subject to closure at short notice. A funeral, a service of thanksgiving or a state occasion can shut it on a day you have already booked, so timed tickets here carry more risk than at a museum.

What a couple pays

Two adults pay 62 pounds. Two adults and two children aged 6 to 17 pay 90 pounds. The same family inside the summer window paid 78.76 pounds, a saving of a little over 11 pounds.

The Abbey's page does not say whether the summer reduction will return in 2027, so treat 31 pounds as the standing adult price.

Sources: westminster-abbey.org, westminster-abbey.org, westminster-abbey.org.

posts.title: Fort Santiago tickets 2026: 75 pesos for adults
posts.summary: Fort Santiago in Intramuros charges 75 pesos for regular entry in 2026 and 50 pesos for students, senior citizens and persons with disability, according to the Intramuros Administration.
posts.body:
Fort Santiago charges 75 pesos for a regular adult ticket in 2026, according to the Intramuros Administration's own hours and fees page. Students, senior citizens and persons with disability pay 50 pesos. That makes it one of the cheapest headline attractions in any Asian capital, and the fee is the same whether bought at the gate or in advance.

The other Intramuros tickets

The same page lists paid access at the Centro de Turismo Intramuros at 150 pesos regular and 120 pesos for students, senior citizens and persons with disability, while the visitor centre and museum areas there are marked free access. Baluarte de San Diego and Casa Manila Museum are listed with opening hours but no admission fee shown on that page, so budget for them separately at the door rather than assuming they are free.

Hours are the thing that catches people

Fort Santiago runs Monday to Friday from 8:00 in the morning to 10:00 at night with last entry at 8:00, and Saturday and Sunday from 6:00 in the morning to 10:00 at night with last entry at 8:30. Casa Manila, the Centro de Turismo and Museo de Intramuros are all closed on Mondays, so a Monday visit is Fort Santiago and walls only.

What a family pays

Two adults and two students at Fort Santiago pay 75 plus 75 plus 50 plus 50, which is 250 pesos. Adding paid access at the Centro de Turismo for all four adds 150 plus 150 plus 120 plus 120, or 540 pesos, taking the day to 790 pesos.

The page does not publish a child rate distinct from the student rate, so families with young children should expect to be charged one of the two published figures.

Sources: intramuros.gov.ph, intramuros.gov.ph, intramuros.gov.ph.

posts.title: Le Jardin Secret tickets 2026: 100 dirhams for the garden
posts.summary: Le Jardin Secret in Marrakech charges 100 dirhams for garden entry in 2026, 80 for visitors up to 24 and 50 for Moroccan citizens, with the tower a separate 40 dirhams.
posts.body:
Le Jardin Secret charges 100 dirhams for full price garden entry in 2026, according to the garden's own English site. Visitors up to 24 years old pay 80 dirhams. Moroccan citizens pay 50 dirhams. Groups of 15 or more pay 80 dirhams per person, and an annual membership is 500 dirhams, which pays for itself on the fifth visit.

The tower is a separate ticket

Access to the tower costs a further 40 dirhams at full price and 30 dirhams at the reduced rate, which covers visitors up to 24, Moroccan citizens and groups of 10 or more. The site also states that the tower visit is prohibited for children under 6, so a family with a toddler cannot all go up regardless of what they pay.

Who gets in free

The garden lists free entry for children under 12, for people with reduced mobility including wheelchair users and blind visitors with a companion, for members, for tourism professionals and for press on written request. A family with two children under 12 therefore pays only for the adults on the garden ticket.

Hours and what a couple pays

Opening is every day, 9:30 to 6:30 in February and October, 9:30 to 7:30 from March to September, 9:30 to 6:00 from November to January and 9:30 to 4:30 during Ramadan, with last entry 30 minutes before closing. Two adults doing garden and tower pay 100 plus 100 plus 40 plus 40, which is 280 dirhams. Two adults with two children under 12 in the garden alone pay 200 dirhams.

The site does not say whether children aged 6 to 11, who enter the garden free, still pay the 40 dirhams for the tower.

Sources: lejardinsecretmarrakech.com, lejardinsecretmarrakech.com, lejardinsecretmarrakech.com.

posts.title: Museo de Antioquia tickets 2026: 46,000 pesos for foreigners
posts.summary: Museo de Antioquia in Medellin charges 46,000 Colombian pesos for foreign visitors in 2026 and 18,000 for Colombian nationals, according to its own online ticket shop.
posts.body:
Museo de Antioquia charges 46,000 Colombian pesos for foreign visitors in 2026 and 18,000 pesos for Colombian nationals, according to the museum's own online ticket shop, where the entry product is sold as two separate variants labelled extranjeros and nacionales. That is a gap of 28,000 pesos on a single admission, and it is applied by nationality rather than by residence.

Buying online is a reservation, not a ticket

The shop describes the purchase as a digital reservation that has to be claimed at the museum ticket window, presenting the name it was registered under, an identification document and the confirmation email, within one month of buying. So an online purchase does not let you skip the desk, and a booking made for someone else under the wrong name is a problem at the door rather than a formality.

Opening days

The museum's visit page gives Monday to Saturday 9:40 in the morning to 5:30 in the afternoon, and Sundays and public holidays 9:40 to 4:30. It closes on 1 January, 1 May and 25 December. Unlike most Colombian museums it does not close on Mondays, which makes it a useful fallback on a day when the rest of the city's cultural sites are shut.

What a couple pays

Two foreign visitors pay 92,000 pesos. A Colombian couple pay 36,000. A mixed couple pay 64,000. At roughly 4,000 pesos to the dollar that is about 23 dollars for two foreigners, still modest by museum standards.

The museum's rates page presents its full table only as an image, so published student, senior and child prices could not be read from the official page and are not stated here.

Sources: tiendamuseodeantioquia.co, tiendamuseodeantioquia.co, museodeantioquia.co.

posts.title: Frida Kahlo Museum tickets 2026: 320 pesos general admission
posts.summary: The Frida Kahlo Museum charges 320 pesos general admission in 2026 and 160 for Mexican residents, and sells no tickets at the door, according to its own visit page.
posts.body:
The Frida Kahlo Museum, the Casa Azul in Coyoacan, charges 320 pesos for general admission in 2026, according to the museum's own visit page. Mexican residents with official identification pay 160 pesos. Students and teachers with a valid credential pay 60 pesos, as do guides and tour operators with official identification. Adults over 65 and children aged 6 to 12 pay 30 pesos. People with disabilities and children under 6 enter free.

There is no box office

The visit page states plainly that the museum does not sell at the ticket window. Every ticket has to be bought in advance online, which means turning up in Coyoacan without a booking is a wasted trip rather than a queue. This is the single most expensive mistake at this museum, because the house is small and demand routinely exceeds the slots released.

Closure dates to avoid

The museum lists full closures on 1 May, 16 September, 8 December, 25 December and 1 January 2027. It also runs shortened hours of 10:00 to 14:00 on 15 September and on 24 and 31 December. Those short days cut the number of entry slots, so they sell out earlier than an ordinary day.

What a family pays

Two foreign adults with children aged 8 and 10 pay 320 plus 320 plus 30 plus 30, which is 700 pesos. Two Mexican resident adults with the same children pay 380 pesos. A student couple with credentials pay 120 pesos, less than a third of one general ticket.

The museum's page does not describe how far ahead tickets are released or how entry times are allocated, so the practical booking window is not knowable from the official page.

Sources: museofridakahlo.org.mx, museofridakahlo.org.mx, museofridakahlo.org.mx.

posts.title: Pinacoteca di Brera tickets 2026: 20 euros full price
posts.summary: The Pinacoteca di Brera in Milan charges 20 euros full price in 2026 and 4 euros for visitors aged 18 to 25, with booking obligatory, according to its own admission page.
posts.body:
The Pinacoteca di Brera charges 20 euros for full price admission in 2026 under the Grande Brera ticket, according to the gallery's own admission page. Visitors aged 18 to 25 pay 4 euros, a reduction of 80 percent that is unusually steep even by Italian state museum standards. The ticket covers the integrated Grande Brera collection rather than the picture gallery alone.

Who pays nothing

The same page lists free entry for under 18s, for people with disabilities holding the relevant Italian documentation, for teachers in Italian state schools, for students and faculty on Italian architecture, cultural heritage, design and art history courses, for licensed tour guides and interpreters, for accredited journalists, for Ministry of Culture staff, for ICOM members and for holders of the Lombardy museum pass. It also gives free admission on the first Sunday of every month.

Booking is not optional

The gallery states that reservation is obligatory and gives a call centre on +39 02 72105 141 open daily from 9:00 to 18:00 alongside the online ticket shop. Audio guides are 5 euros in Italian, English, French, German and Russian, and radio guides for groups are 2 euros including disposable earpieces.

What a couple and a family pay

Two adults pay 40 euros, or 50 euros with an audio guide each. Two adults with two children under 18 also pay 40 euros, because the children are free. Two adults with two university students aged 18 to 25 pay 48 euros.

The page does not say whether the obligatory reservation carries a booking fee, or whether the free first Sunday still needs one, so allow for both.

Sources: pinacotecabrera.org, pinacotecabrera.org, pinacotecabrera.org.

posts.title: Rose Hall Great House tickets 2026: 30 US dollars by day
posts.summary: Rose Hall Great House near Montego Bay charges 30 US dollars per adult for the day tour in 2026 and 35 for the night tour, with children at 10 and 15, per its own tour page.
posts.body:
Rose Hall Great House charges 30 US dollars per adult for the day tour in 2026 and 10 US dollars per child aged 12 and under, according to the property's own tour page. The night tour is 35 US dollars per adult and 15 US dollars per child. Prices are quoted in US dollars rather than Jamaican dollars, which is standard for the Montego Bay tourist corridor.

The two tours run on different days

Day tours run Mondays to Saturdays from 9:15 in the morning to 4:00 in the afternoon. Night tours run Wednesdays to Saturdays only, with departures at 6:00, 6:30, 7:00, 7:30 and 8:00 in the evening. That means Sunday and Monday and Tuesday evenings have no tour at all, which is the detail most likely to cost a cruise passenger or a short stay visitor a wasted taxi fare from the resort strip.

How long you get

Each tour is described as lasting approximately 45 minutes to an hour. Set against a 30 dollar adult ticket that works out at roughly 30 to 40 dollars per hour of guided time, before whatever the transfer from Montego Bay costs, which is not included.

What a family pays

Two adults and two children aged 12 and under pay 30 plus 30 plus 10 plus 10, which is 80 US dollars on the day tour. The same four on the night tour pay 100 US dollars. Two adults alone pay 60 by day and 70 at night.

The tour page does not state whether Jamaican general consumption tax is included in the quoted prices or added at the desk.

Sources: rosehall.com, rosehall.com, rosehall.com.

posts.title: Nymphenburg Palace tickets 2026: 10 euros for the palace
posts.summary: Nymphenburg Palace in Munich charges 10 euros for palace entry in 2026, or 20 euros for the summer combination ticket, with under 18s free, per the Bavarian palace administration.
posts.body:
Nymphenburg Palace charges 10 euros for a palace ticket in 2026, with a reduced rate of 9 euros, according to the Bavarian palace administration's own admission page. Children and young people under 18 are admitted free of charge, and students over 18 at general or vocational schools also enter free with a valid student card, which makes this one of the cheaper major palaces in Europe for a family.

The combination ticket changes with the season

The combination ticket covering the palace, the Marstallmuseum and the park palaces is 20 euros full price and 18 euros reduced in summer, defined as 1 April to 15 October. In winter, from 16 October to 31 March, it drops to 16 euros full and 14 euros reduced, because part of the park estate is closed. Buying the combination in winter therefore costs 4 euros less but covers less ground.

Timed entry applies to the palace

The administration states that for Nymphenburg Palace only tickets with time slots are available, and that admission is possible up to a maximum of one hour after the time chosen. Arrive more than an hour late and the ticket is not guaranteed, which matters if you are combining the palace with the park in one afternoon.

What a family pays

Two adults and two children under 18 pay 20 euros for palace entry alone, because the children are free. The same family on the summer combination ticket pays 40 euros, and on the winter version 32 euros.

The admission page does not list opening hours or closure days, so those need checking separately before booking a time slot.

Sources: schloss-nymphenburg.de, schloss-nymphenburg.de, schloss-nymphenburg.de.

posts.title: Giraffe Centre tickets 2026: 1,500 shillings for non resident adults
posts.summary: The Giraffe Centre in Nairobi charges 1,500 Kenyan shillings for non resident adults in 2026 and 750 for non resident children, with residents at 400 and 200, per its own site.
posts.body:
The Giraffe Centre in Karen charges 1,500 Kenyan shillings for a non resident adult in 2026 and 750 shillings for a non resident child aged 3 to 12, according to the centre's own website. Residents pay 400 shillings as adults and 200 shillings for children aged 3 to 12. Children below 3 years of age are free. At roughly 130 shillings to the dollar the non resident adult price is a little under 12 dollars.

Resident means East African, not just Kenyan

The centre defines the resident charge as applying to guests who are either citizens of, or hold a work permit for, any of the East African Community countries. That is a wider definition than most Kenyan attractions use and it is worth knowing if anyone in the party holds a Ugandan, Tanzanian or Rwandan passport, because the difference is 1,100 shillings per adult.

Opening and timing

The centre states that it is open daily from 9:00 in the morning to 5:00 in the afternoon. Feeding is spread through the day rather than restricted to set sessions, but the giraffes are most active early, so the first two hours are the practical window. There is no published online versus gate price difference, so the figures above are what you pay at the entrance.

What a family pays

Two non resident adults and two children aged 3 to 12 pay 1,500 plus 1,500 plus 750 plus 750, which is 4,500 shillings, about 35 dollars. A resident family of the same shape pays 1,200 shillings.

The centre publishes prices only in shillings and does not state whether cards are accepted, so the dollar cost moves with the exchange rate and cash may be needed.

Sources: giraffecentre.org, giraffecentre.org, giraffecentre.org.

posts.title: Pompeii tickets 2026: 20 euros for the site alone
posts.summary: A Pompeii only ticket is 20 euros in 2026 on the park's own ticket page, with 25 euros for the version that adds the suburban villas and Boscoreale.
posts.body:
A ticket to Pompeii alone costs 20 euros in 2026, according to the archaeological park's own timetables and tickets page, which lists prices dated 12 January 2026.

Three different tickets

The same official page lists 25 euros for Pompeii together with the suburban villas and Boscoreale, and 30 euros for Pompeii Plus, a three day pass that also covers Oplontis, Villa Arianna, Villa San Marco, the Archaeological Museum of Stabiae and Boscoreale. The smaller sites on their own are 8 euros each. Villa Arianna and Villa San Marco at Stabiae are shown as free. An annual MyPompeii pass is 45 euros, or 10 euros at the reduced rate.

Reduced and free entry

The park publishes a 2 euro reduced rate per site for EU citizens aged 18 to 24 and for eligible residents from outside the EU. Entry is free on the first Sunday of every month, which is also the day the site fills up fastest.

What a couple pays, and the rules that cost money

Two adults on the basic ticket pay 40 euros, and 50 euros if they take the 25 euro version for the villas. The page states a daily cap of 20,000 entries and nominative tickets, so a spare ticket bought for someone who then cannot come is not simply handed on. Winter hours, from 15 October to 14 March, are 9am to 5pm with last entry at 3.30pm, and summer hours are 9am to 7pm with last entry at 5.30pm. The page does not say whether the online booking system adds a service fee on top of these prices.

Sources: pompeiisites.org.

posts.title: National WWII Museum tickets 2026: 37 dollars adult, 9 for the films
posts.summary: Adult admission to the National WWII Museum is 37 dollars in 2026 on the museum's own visit page, and the two theatre experiences are charged on top.
posts.body:
Adult admission to the National WWII Museum in New Orleans is 37 dollars in 2026, according to the museum's own visit page, and the films inside cost extra.

The published rates

The museum lists 34 dollars for seniors aged 65 and over, 27 dollars for students from kindergarten through college, 27 dollars for military visitors with identification, and free entry for children under 5, for WWII veterans and for members. Nothing on the page suggests a different price at the door than online.

The add ons that catch people out

General admission does not include the two theatre experiences. Beyond All Boundaries is 9 dollars, the Priddy Family Freedom Theater is 9 dollars, and a combined ticket for both is 12 dollars. A second day pass is 15 dollars. The USS Tang submarine experience is included with admission.

A family of four, and the closed days

Two adults and two students on general admission come to 128 dollars. Adding the 12 dollar film combination for all four takes it to 176 dollars, and a second day for everyone adds 60 dollars more. The museum is open daily from 9am to 5pm and is closed on Mardi Gras Day, Thanksgiving Day, Christmas Eve and Christmas Day, which matters in a city where Mardi Gras is exactly when visitors are in town. Beyond All Boundaries runs on the hour from 10am to 4pm, so a late afternoon arrival can miss it.

Sources: nationalww2museum.org.

posts.title: Empire State Building tickets 2026: from 44 dollars plus a 5 dollar booking charge
posts.summary: Main deck tickets start at 44 dollars in 2026 on the observatory's own booking page, with a 5 dollar booking charge added and 79 dollars for both decks.
posts.body:
Empire State Building main deck tickets start at 44 dollars in 2026, and the observatory's own booking page adds a 5 dollar booking charge on top.

The tiers

According to the building's own ticket page, the 86th floor main deck starts at 44 dollars, while the combined 86th and 102nd floor ticket starts at 79 dollars. Express passes that skip the queues start at 85 dollars for the 86th floor and 120 dollars for both decks. A cheaper option described as the best value ticket starts at 39 dollars. Guided premium tours start at 175 dollars, an all access tour is 500 dollars, and a proposal package is 1,000 dollars.

What the page does not say

No child or senior price is published on that page, and every figure is quoted as a starting price, which means it moves with the date and the time slot. New York locals are offered 25 percent off. Reservations are required, though the page notes that tickets can also be bought in person at the ticket office.

A couple and a family

Two adults on the main deck at the lowest advertised price come to 88 dollars before the booking charge, and a family of four to 176 dollars. Choosing the two deck ticket instead takes a couple to 158 dollars, and the express version of it to 240 dollars. It is not clear from the page whether the 5 dollar booking charge applies once per order or once per ticket, so budget for the worse case.

Sources: esbnyc.com.

posts.title: Musée Matisse Nice tickets 2026: 12 euros, or 15 for every city museum
posts.summary: The Musée Matisse charges 12 euros in 2026 on its own practical information page, while a four day pass to all Nice municipal museums is 15 euros.
posts.body:
The Musée Matisse in Nice charges 12 euros for a single adult ticket in 2026, according to the museum's own practical information page, but 15 euros buys four days of every municipal museum in the city.

One museum or all of them

The official page lists 12 euros for individual entry and 9 euros per person for groups of ten or more, with advance reservation required. The four day Pass Musées de Nice is 15 euros, or 10 euros per person for groups. Anyone planning to see a second municipal museum as well passes the break even point immediately, since two single tickets already cost 24 euros.

Who pays nothing

The museum lists free entry for visitors under 18, students, unemployed visitors, people receiving RSA, ASS or ASPA, disabled visitors, ICOM and ICOMOS members, journalists, teachers and museum guides. Residents of Nice and the neighbouring communes aged 18 and over also enter free with identification and proof of address.

A family visit and the closed day

Two adults with two teenagers pay 24 euros for this one museum, or 30 euros for two four day passes, because the teenagers are free either way. Opening hours are 10am to 5pm from 1 November to 31 March and 10am to 6pm from 1 April to 31 October. The museum closes on Tuesdays and on 1 January, Easter Sunday, 1 May and 25 December. The page publishes no senior rate and no separate online price.

Sources: musee-matisse-nice.org.

posts.title: Osaka Castle tickets 2026: 1,200 yen for the main tower
posts.summary: Adult entry to the Osaka Castle main tower is 1,200 yen in 2026 on the castle's own guide page, with students at 600 yen and middle school age and under free.
posts.body:
Adult entry to the Osaka Castle main tower is 1,200 yen in 2026, according to the castle's own visitor guide, where the fee table carries the date 1 April 2025.

The fee table

The same page lists 600 yen for high school and university students on production of proof, and free entry for middle school students and younger, again with proof of age. Osaka City residents aged 65 and over enter free with proof, as do holders of disability, welfare or atomic bomb survivor handbooks, with one carer also admitted free. The Mirairo ID app is accepted in place of a paper handbook.

Timing and booking

The tower opens from 9:00 to 18:00 with last admission at 17:30, and closes from 28 December to 1 January. The castle site points visitors to a reservation website where entry tickets can be bought in advance. The published fee is the same figure either way, so advance booking buys time rather than money in the cherry blossom weeks when the queue is longest.

What a family pays

Two adults with two children of primary or middle school age pay 2,400 yen in total, because the children are free. Swap one child for a high school student and the total becomes 3,000 yen. A couple on their own also pay 2,400 yen. What the page does not make clear is whether the April 2025 fee table is still the current one later in 2026, so check the date line above the prices before budgeting.

Sources: osakacastle.net.

posts.title: Eiffel Tower tickets 2026: 23.50 euros to the second floor, 36.70 to the top
posts.summary: The tower's own rates page puts an adult lift ticket to the second floor at 23.50 euros in 2026 and the lift to the top at 36.70 euros, with stairs from 14.80.
posts.body:
An adult lift ticket to the Eiffel Tower's second floor costs 23.50 euros in 2026 and the lift to the top costs 36.70 euros, according to the tower's own rates page.

Four ways up, four prices

The official page lists 23.50 euros for the lift to the second floor, 36.70 euros for the lift to the top, 14.80 euros for the stairs to the second floor, and 28.00 euros for the stairs followed by the lift to the top. Walking the first stage and finishing by lift saves 8.70 euros against the full lift ticket.

Youth and child rates

Visitors aged 12 to 24 pay 11.80 euros for the lift to the second floor, 18.40 euros to the top, 7.40 euros for the stairs, and 14.00 euros for the stairs and lift combination. Children aged 4 to 11 pay 6.00, 9.20, 3.80 and 7.00 euros respectively for the same four tickets.

What a family pays

Two adults and two children aged 8 and 10 going to the top by lift pay 91.80 euros. The same family stopping at the second floor pays 59.00 euros, and walking up to the second floor brings it down to 37.20 euros. A couple climbing the stairs pay 29.60 euros between them. The rates page shows no separate price for buying at the ticket desk, so booking online appears to secure a time slot rather than a discount, and the tower sells out well ahead in summer.

Sources: toureiffel.paris.

posts.title: Petra club car tickets 2026: 15 dinars to the Treasury
posts.summary: A club car from the Petra visitor centre to the Treasury is 15 Jordanian dinars in 2026 on the site authority's own fees page, with guides from 50 dinars.
posts.body:
A club car from the Petra visitor centre to the Treasury costs 15 Jordanian dinars in 2026, according to the Petra site authority's own fees page.

Rides inside the site

The official page lists 15 dinars for the four kilometre trip from the visitor centre to the Treasury and 25 dinars for the eight kilometre version there and back. Deeper in the basin, the one kilometre run from the Petra theatre to Qaser Albint is 10 dinars, or 15 dinars in both directions. All of these sit on top of the entry ticket rather than inside it.

Guides and viewpoints

The same page prices a licensed guide at 50 dinars for the main trail, and at 100 dinars for the main trail with either the High Place or the Monastery added. A ticket for the viewpoints opposite the Treasury is 15 dinars.

Two rules worth knowing

The authority states that the Jordan Pass does not cover the Petra by Night show, and that a daylight ticket is required in order to attend it. Children under 10 go to Petra by Night free, and children under 12 enter free during the day. A couple who ride in, walk out and hire a guide for the main trail spend 80 dinars between them on extras alone, or 110 dinars once they add the Treasury viewpoint. The page sets out the rules for Petra by Night without printing its ticket price, so that one figure still has to come from the ticket office.

Sources: visitpetra.jo.

posts.title: Phuket Elephant Sanctuary tickets 2026: from 1,900 baht
posts.summary: The sanctuary's own page prices the canopy walkway from 1,900 baht in 2026 and the half day programme from 3,000 baht, with no child rate published.
posts.body:
A visit to the Phuket Elephant Sanctuary starts at 1,900 baht in 2026, according to the sanctuary's own programme page.

Two programmes, two prices

The official page prices the canopy walkway tour from 1,900 baht for one and a half hours, and the half day programme from 3,000 baht for three and a half hours. Both are listed as suitable for all ages. Places are sold through the sanctuary's own booking calendar rather than at a gate, so there is no walk up price to compare an online rate against.

What is not published

The page shows no separate child rate and no senior rate, and both figures are given as starting prices, which normally means the amount charged shifts with the date picked in the booking calendar. Longer and volunteer options are referred to elsewhere on the site without a price attached to them.

A couple and a family

Two adults on the half day programme pay 6,000 baht at the starting rate, and a family of four pays 12,000 baht. The shorter canopy walkway brings that same family to 7,600 baht. Because the sanctuary publishes only starting prices, treat these totals as the floor rather than the final bill, and confirm the exact amount in the booking calendar for the date you want.

Sources: phuketelephantsanctuary.org.

posts.title: Clérigos Tower tickets 2026: 10 euros for the tower and museum
posts.summary: The Clérigos Tower day ticket is 10 euros in 2026 on the monument's own ticket office page, with students at 7 euros and children up to 10 free.
posts.body:
A day ticket for the Clérigos Tower and its museum in Porto costs 10 euros in 2026, according to the monument's own ticket office page.

Day and night prices

The official page lists 10 euros general admission, 7 euros for students on production of identification, and free entry for children up to 10 years old. A night ticket covering 7pm to 11pm is 5 euros, free again for children up to 10, but it is only sold on special dates around Easter, in summer and at Christmas, so it is not something to plan a trip around.

Combined tickets

The same page prices the tower with the Stock Exchange Palace and MMIPO at 25 euros, the tower with Serralves at 27.20 euros, and the tower with the SPIRITUS multimedia show at 19 euros. Porto Card holders are given 50 percent off.

Timing and a worked example

Opening is 9am to 7pm, extended to 11pm in the Easter, summer and Christmas periods, with last entry always 30 minutes before closing. Two adults pay 20 euros, and a family of two adults with two children under 10 pays the same 20 euros. A couple taking the Serralves combination instead pay 54.40 euros. The page lists no senior rate, and it does not say whether school pupils over 10 count as students for the 7 euro price.

Sources: torredosclerigos.pt.

posts.title: Jewish Museum in Prague tickets 2026: 600 CZK for the full circuit
posts.summary: The museum's own admission page puts an adult circuit ticket at 600 CZK in 2026, valid for three opening days across five synagogues and the Old Jewish Cemetery.
posts.body:
A full adult ticket to the Jewish Museum in Prague is 600 CZK in 2026, according to the museum's own admission page, and it covers five synagogues and the Old Jewish Cemetery rather than one building.

The published prices

The official page lists 600 CZK for adults, 400 CZK for students under 26, 200 CZK for children aged 7 to 15, free entry for children up to 6, and 100 CZK for disability card holders. The Prague Visitor Pass and the Cool Pass are both accepted for free entry.

Rules that cost people money

The museum states that tickets are valid for three opening days, so a circuit started late in the afternoon can be finished later in the trip. Ticket sales stop 30 minutes before closing, and the museum is closed on Saturdays, which catches out visitors who assume a Saturday morning slot. Discounted and bonus tickets are issued only in person at the visitor centre on Maiselova, not through the website.

A family of four

Two adults with children aged 9 and 12 pay 1,600 CZK in total. Two adults on their own pay 1,200 CZK, and a couple in their early twenties holding student cards pay 800 CZK. The page also shows a 30 percent discount for holders of an annual Lítačka coupon, quoted as 280 CZK against 420 CZK, and it is not clear which ticket those two figures apply to.

Sources: jewishmuseum.cz.

posts.title: Scape Park tickets 2026: 129 dollars full admission
posts.summary: Full admission to Scape Park at Cap Cana is 129 US dollars in 2026 on the park's own rates page, rising to 169 with buggies and 189 for the VIP option.
posts.body:
Full admission to Scape Park at Cap Cana, the excursion most Punta Cana visitors book for the Hoyo Azul cenote, costs 129 US dollars in 2026, according to the park's own rates page.

The four rates

The official page lists full admission at 129 dollars, full admission with buggies at 169 dollars, full admission with the Sunshine Cruise at 169 dollars, and the Juanillo VIP option at 189 dollars. The park runs from 9am to 5pm daily with the attractions themselves closing at 4.30pm, so a late morning arrival quietly cuts into what the ticket buys.

What the page leaves out

No child price is published on the rates page, and there is no itemised list showing which activities sit inside full admission and which are charged separately. Hoyo Azul is presented as part of the park rather than as its own ticket.

What a couple and a family pay

Two adults on full admission pay 258 dollars. A family of four at the same rate pays 516 dollars, and the buggy version takes that to 676 dollars. Those are the figures to plan against, but because the park publishes no child rate at all, a family should confirm whether children pay the adult price before booking.

Sources: scapepark.com.

posts.title: Kawarau Bridge Bungy tickets 2026: 320 New Zealand dollars
posts.summary: The operator's own site prices the Kawarau Bridge Bungy at 320 New Zealand dollars in 2026, with the Nevis Bungy at 395 and the Nevis Swing at 325.
posts.body:
A jump from the Kawarau Bridge outside Queenstown costs 320 New Zealand dollars in 2026, according to the operator's own website.

The three Queenstown prices

The site lists the Kawarau Bridge Bungy at 320 dollars, the Nevis Bungy at 395 dollars and the Nevis Swing at 325 dollars. Kawarau is the original commercial bungy site and the cheapest of the three, the Nevis is the tall one out in the valley, and the 75 dollar gap between them is what the extra height costs.

What the page does not publish

No youth or child price appears beside those figures, and no price at all is shown for the Ledge, the jump above the town itself. The site also does not state on that page whether photographs and video come with the jump or are sold afterwards, which is the usual place a bungy booking grows.

What two people pay

A couple both jumping at Kawarau pay 640 dollars between them. One Kawarau bungy and one Nevis Swing come to 645 dollars, and two Nevis Bungy jumps come to 790 dollars. Booking runs through the operator's own reservation system or by phone. The three figures above are the adult rates shown on the front of the site, and because youth pricing and the Ledge are not published there, both need checking with the operator directly.

Sources: bungy.co.nz.

posts.title: Galleria Borghese tickets 2026: 18 euros with the booking fee
posts.summary: A full price Galleria Borghese ticket is 18 euros in 2026, made up of 16 euros entry plus a compulsory 2 euro booking fee. Even free under 18 tickets carry the 2 euros.
posts.body:
A full price ticket to the Galleria Borghese in Rome costs 18 euros in 2026, and that figure already includes the compulsory booking fee. According to the official ticket page run by Gebart, the operator that handles admissions for the gallery, the breakdown is 16 euros for entry plus 2 euros as a reservation charge, listed on the page as Intero 18,00 euro.

Reduced and free tickets still cost something

Citizens of the European Union aged 18 to 25 pay a reduced rate the page shows as 2 euros, which is the booking fee alone with no admission charge attached. Visitors under 18 are admitted free, but the same 2 euro reservation charge applies, so a free child ticket is not actually zero. The page lists exemptions from the fee for disabled visitors and their companions, licensed European Union tour guides and accredited journalists. There is also a late entry at 17.45 priced at 13 euros.

The booking rule that costs people money

Advance purchase is mandatory. The gallery runs timed entry in two hour visits with a cap of roughly 180 people per slot, and slots run from 09:00 to 19:00. Turning up on spec is not an option here in the way it is at some Roman sites, and weekend slots go early.

What a family of four pays

Two adults and two children under 18 come to 36 euros for the adults plus 4 euros in booking fees for the children, so 40 euros for one two hour slot. A couple alone pays 36 euros.

What the page does not make clear is whether the 2 euro fee is charged on every route to a ticket or only through the official reseller.

Sources: gebart.it, gebart.it.

posts.title: Gold Museum San Jose tickets 2026: 8,800 colones for foreign adults
posts.summary: Foreign adults pay 8,800 colones at the Museos del Banco Central in San Jose in 2026, against 3,000 colones for Costa Ricans. Under 12s are free and it opens daily.
posts.body:
Foreign adults pay 8,800 colones to enter the Museos del Banco Central de Costa Rica in San Jose in 2026, the underground complex beneath the Plaza de la Cultura that holds the Pre Columbian Gold Museum. According to the museum's own visitor page, the same ticket costs 3,000 colones for Costa Ricans and residents, so a foreign visitor pays close to three times the local rate for the identical rooms.

Student and child rates

Foreign students are listed at 6,950 colones and national students at 1,000 colones, both on presentation of a valid card. Children under 12 enter free, as do Costa Rican senior citizens, tourism guides, members of indigenous communities and ICOM members. The numismatic collection and the temporary exhibition rooms sit inside the same building and are not charged separately.

Opening hours

The page gives hours as Monday to Sunday, 9 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., so the museum opens every day of the week. Nothing on the page mentions timed entry, sold out slots or advance booking, which makes this one of the few well known city museums a traveller can still simply walk into.

A worked example

Two foreign adults with a child of 10 pay 17,600 colones in total, because the child is free. Swap that child for a 15 year old and the bill rises to 26,400 colones unless the teenager can produce a student card, in which case it is 24,550.

What the page does not say is whether the foreign rate can be paid in US dollars at the desk, which is common in San Jose and would move the final figure with the day's exchange rate.

Sources: museosdelbancocentral.org, museosdelbancocentral.org.

posts.title: Waterbom Bali tickets 2026: 630,000 rupiah for an adult day pass
posts.summary: An adult single day pass at Waterbom Bali is 630,000 rupiah in 2026, a child pass 495,000, and a family pass for two adults and two children 2,200,000 rupiah.
posts.body:
An adult single day pass to Waterbom Bali, the water park a short drive from Seminyak in Kuta, costs 630,000 rupiah in 2026 according to the park's own ticket page. A child pass, for ages 2 to 11, is listed at 495,000 rupiah, and a family pass covering two adults and two children is 2,200,000 rupiah.

The upgraded passes

The same page lists an All In Pass at 885,000 rupiah for an adult and 550,000 rupiah for a child, with a family version at 2,875,000 rupiah. There is also a Duo Pass at 1,600,000 rupiah for two people, bundling towels, a locker and a 30 minute foot massage, and a Four Pack at 2,800,000 rupiah with towels, lockers and popcorn. Whether an upgrade pays for itself depends entirely on whether you would have rented a towel and a locker anyway.

Hours and booking

The park lists its hours as every day, 9am to 6pm. Prices are quoted in rupiah only, with no dollar rate published, and the figures shown are the online booking rates. Dates on the booking calendar can show as fully booked, so a family building a whole day around the park should check the date before committing to it.

What two adults and two children pay

The family pass at 2,200,000 rupiah is the cheaper route for that group. The same four bought as two adult and two child tickets comes to 2,250,000 rupiah, so the family pass saves 50,000 rupiah. Upgrading the whole family to the All In Pass takes the day to 2,875,000 rupiah.

What is not published anywhere on the page is a gate price, so the gap between booking online and paying at the entrance is unclear.

Sources: waterbom-bali.com, waterbom-bali.com.

posts.title: Gardens by the Bay tickets 2026: 12 dollars for the Flower Dome
posts.summary: The Flower Dome at Gardens by the Bay is 12 Singapore dollars for an adult in 2026 and 8 for a child or senior, with the two dome combined ticket listed at 34.
posts.body:
A single adult ticket to the Flower Dome at Gardens by the Bay costs 12 Singapore dollars in 2026, according to the attraction's own admission page. Seniors aged 60 and above and children aged 3 to 12 pay 8 dollars for the same conservatory, and those figures appear under both the Singapore resident and the non resident headings, so the Flower Dome on its own is priced the same whoever buys it.

Residency matters on the combined tickets

A ticket covering the Flower Dome and the Cloud Forest is listed at 34 dollars for an adult, 29 for a senior and 26 for a child. The non resident table also carries a 46 dollar adult and 32 dollar child version of what reads as the same pairing, and the page does not spell out which one a foreign visitor is charged. The largest bundle, adding Floral Fantasy and a shuttle, is 73 dollars for a non resident adult and 51 for a child, against 49 and 37 for residents.

What a couple and a family pay

Two adults visiting only the Flower Dome pay 24 dollars, which is the cheapest way into the glasshouses. Two adults and two children doing both conservatories at the 34 dollar rate come to 120 dollars, and at the 46 dollar non resident rate to 156 dollars. Children under 3 are not listed as a paying category at all.

The unclear part is genuine and worth flagging: the official page prints two different prices for what looks like the same two conservatory ticket, and only the checkout will settle which one applies to a visitor from abroad.

Sources: gardensbythebay.com.sg, gardensbythebay.com.sg.

posts.title: Vasa Museum tickets 2026: 240 kronor in summer, 195 in winter
posts.summary: The Vasa Museum in Stockholm charges 240 kronor for an adult from May to September in 2026 and 195 kronor the rest of the year. Under 18s are free in both seasons.
posts.body:
An adult ticket to the Vasa Museum in Stockholm costs 240 Swedish kronor from May to September in 2026 and 195 kronor for the rest of the year, according to the museum's own hours and admission page. That seasonal split is the most useful thing to know about the price, because the same warship costs 45 kronor more in the months when almost everyone goes.

Children go free

Visitors aged 18 and under are admitted free in both seasons, which makes the Vasa unusually cheap for a family by central Stockholm standards. The page notes that children aged 12 and under must be accompanied by an adult at all times. No separate student or senior rate is published there.

Hours and payment

From September to May the museum opens 10:00 to 17:00 daily, with Wednesdays running until 20:00. In June, July and August it opens much earlier and longer, 08:30 to 18:00. The museum also states that it accepts card payment only, so arriving with a pocket of kronor in cash is a wasted errand.

A worked example

Two adults and two children aged 9 and 14 pay 480 kronor in high season and 390 kronor in low season, since both children enter free either way. A couple who visit in October rather than July save 90 kronor between them for the identical exhibition and the identical ship.

What the page does not state is whether the summer rate runs by calendar month or by a published set of dates, which matters if you are booking at the edges of May or September.

Sources: vasamuseet.se, vasamuseet.se.

posts.title: Sydney Opera House tour tickets 2026: 50 dollars ahead, 55 on the day
posts.summary: The standard Sydney Opera House guided tour is 50 Australian dollars for an adult booked ahead in 2026 and 55 on the day, with a family ticket at 130 or 145.
posts.body:
The standard Sydney Opera House guided tour costs 50 Australian dollars for an adult booked in advance in 2026 and 55 dollars bought on the day, according to the Opera House's own tour page. That 5 dollar gap runs through every category on the list, which makes booking ahead the simplest saving available at the building.

Child, concession and family rates

A child ticket is 30 dollars in advance and 35 on the day, and the page defines a child as 5 to 15 years of age, with children under 5 free of charge. Concession is 40 dollars in advance and 45 on the day, available to holders of an Australian Seniors Card, Australian pensioners and full time students aged 16 and over. The family ticket, described as 2 adults and 2 children aged 15 and under, is 130 dollars in advance and 145 on the day.

What the ticket actually buys

The tour runs 60 minutes and is offered in English, French, German, Japanese, Mandarin Chinese, Korean and Spanish. It is a guided walk through the building, not a performance, so anyone hoping to hear an orchestra is buying a different ticket entirely.

A worked example

Two adults and two children aged 8 and 12 pay 130 dollars on the family ticket booked ahead, against 160 dollars for four separate advance tickets, so the family ticket saves 30 dollars. Leave it to the day and the family ticket costs 145 dollars.

What the page does not settle is whether the higher on the day price applies only at the box office or also to a same day online booking made from the queue.

Sources: sydneyoperahouse.com, sydneyoperahouse.com.

posts.title: Tel Aviv Museum of Art tickets 2026: 55 shekels for an adult
posts.summary: Regular admission to the Tel Aviv Museum of Art is 55 shekels in 2026, students 45 and seniors 27, with everyone up to 18 admitted free on the museum's own figures.
posts.body:
Regular admission to the Tel Aviv Museum of Art costs 55 shekels in 2026, according to the museum's own visitor page. Students pay 45 shekels, and senior citizens and visitors with disabilities pay 27 shekels, roughly half the standard rate. Children and young people up to the age of 18 enter free.

Who else gets in free

The free list published by the museum is longer than most. It covers active duty soldiers, national service volunteers and museum members, and extends to journalists, licensed tour guides and ICOM members on presentation of valid identification. The page is blunt that discounts are given only on presentation of a valid certificate or card, so a student who left the card at the hotel pays the full 55 shekels.

One entry, not a day pass

The museum states that the entrance fee provides a single entry to the museum. That matters more than it sounds, because the collection is spread across the main building and the Herta and Paul Amir wing, and stepping out for lunch and coming back is not a free move.

A worked example

Two adults with teenagers aged 14 and 17 pay 110 shekels in total, since both young people are free. Two adults with an adult student in the party pay 155 shekels. Two pensioners pay 54 shekels between them, which is less than one full adult ticket.

What the visitor page does not give is the opening days or the weekly closed day, so anyone planning a specific afternoon should confirm the hours separately before travelling across town.

Sources: tamuseum.org.il, tamuseum.org.il.

posts.title: Tokyo Skytree tickets 2026: from 1,800 yen online, 500 more at the counter
posts.summary: Tokyo Skytree Tembo Deck tickets start at 1,800 yen for an adult online in 2026, with a 500 yen per ticket service fee added at the fourth floor counter.
posts.body:
An adult ticket to the Tembo Deck at Tokyo Skytree starts at 1,800 yen in 2026 when bought online, according to the tower's own ticket page. The combined ticket covering the Tembo Deck at 350 metres and the Tembo Galleria at 450 metres starts at 3,000 yen for an adult. Both are quoted as From prices, because Skytree varies the rate by date.

The 500 yen you can avoid

The page states plainly that a 500 yen service fee per ticket is added for purchases made at the fourth floor ticket counter or the ticket vending machines. For a family of four that is 2,000 yen handed over for the sake of not booking ahead, and it is the clearest avoidable cost at the tower.

Child prices

Children aged 6 to 14 start at 900 yen for the Tembo Deck and 1,500 yen for the combined ticket. Admission is free for young children aged 5 and under. Because the rate moves with the date, the number shown for a July Saturday will not be the number shown for a wet Tuesday in February.

A worked example

Two adults and two children aged 8 and 11 visiting the Tembo Deck pay from 5,400 yen booked online, and from 7,400 yen if all four tickets are bought at the counter on arrival. Going all the way up to the Galleria takes the same family to at least 9,000 yen online.

What the page does not publish is the ceiling. The From wording means peak dates cost more than the headline, but the top of the range is never stated.

Sources: en.tokyo-skytree.jp, en.tokyo-skytree.jp.

posts.title: Monkey Forest Ubud tickets 2026: 130,000 rupiah for an adult
posts.summary: The Sacred Monkey Forest Sanctuary charges 130,000 rupiah for adults and 100,000 for children in 2026, with last entrance at 17:00 on an 18:00 close.
posts.body:
The Sacred Monkey Forest Sanctuary in Ubud charges 130,000 rupiah for an adult in 2026, according to the sanctuary's own visit page, and 100,000 rupiah for a child. It is the one paid attraction almost every Ubud itinerary includes.

What the gate charges

The published fees are IDR 130.000 for adults and IDR 100.000 for children. The site does not advertise a lower price for buying ahead, so the online price and the counter price appear to be the same number. Tickets are sold through the Megatix link on the official site and at the entrance.

The hours that cost people money

The forest is open 9:00 to 18:00, but the official page states that the last entrance is 17:00. Arriving at half past five means the ticket window is shut and the visit is gone. No weekly closing day is published, so the risk here is time of day rather than day of week.

Worked example

Two adults and two children pay 130,000 plus 130,000 plus 100,000 plus 100,000, which is 460,000 rupiah. A couple pays 260,000 rupiah. Neither figure covers the banana packs sold inside or the car parking outside.

Still unclear: the page does not give an age range for the child ticket or say whether infants enter free.

Sources: https://monkeyforestubud.com/visit/

posts.title: Capilano Suspension Bridge tickets 2026: 75 dollars for an adult
posts.summary: A day ticket is 75 Canadian dollars for adults and 28 for children aged 6 to 12 in 2026, with a 25 percent twilight rate after 5pm.
posts.body:
A day ticket to Capilano Suspension Bridge Park costs 75 Canadian dollars for an adult in 2026, according to the park's own tickets page. That is the headline number and the one most visitors pay.

The full price list

The park publishes Adult at 75.00, Senior aged 65 and over at 70.00, Student aged 18 and over at 64.00, Youth aged 13 to 17 at 49.00 and Child aged 6 to 12 at 28.00. Children 5 and under are free. No separate gate price is published, so booking online costs the same as arriving.

The twilight rate nobody notices

Entry from 5pm until close carries a 25 percent saving, listed as 56.25 for an adult, 52.50 for a senior, 48.00 for a student, 36.75 for a youth and 21.00 for a child. The park shows this running to October 8, 2026. It also warns that date and time changes are not permitted once a ticket is bought, so a booking made for the wrong day is money gone.

Worked example

Two adults and two children aged 6 to 12 pay 75 plus 75 plus 28 plus 28, which is 206 Canadian dollars. The same family arriving after 5pm pays 154.50, a saving of 51.50. A couple pays 150 by day and 112.50 at twilight.

Still unclear: the tickets page lists the twilight window but not the park's daily opening hour, so the length of a standard visit is not fixed.

Sources: https://www.capilanobridge.com/tickets.html

posts.title: Doge's Palace tickets 2026: 35 euros, or 30 booked a month ahead
posts.summary: Entry to the Doge's Palace is 35 euros in 2026 as part of the St Mark's Square Museums ticket, dropping to 30 euros only if you book at least 30 days ahead.
posts.body:
Entry to the Doge's Palace in Venice costs 35 euros in 2026, and there is no palace only ticket. According to the city museums' own ticket page, the 35 euro St Mark's Square Museums ticket covers the Doge's Palace, Museum Correr, the National Archaeological Museum of Venice and the Monumental Rooms of the Marciana National Library.

The five euros you can save

The same page lists 30 euros as a price reserved only to the online purchase at least 30 days prior to the visit date. Book inside that window and you pay the full 35. This is the only published difference between buying online and buying on the day, and it rewards planning a month out rather than a morning out.

Who pays 15 euros

The reduced rate of 15 euros applies to children aged 6 to 14, students aged 15 to 25, visitors over 65, holders of the Venice Rolling Card and ISIC holders. Children aged 0 to 5 enter free, as do Venetian residents and disabled visitors with a helper. The palace was showing hours of 09:00 to 19:00.

Worked example

Two adults and two children aged 6 to 14 pay 35 plus 35 plus 15 plus 15, which is 100 euros. If the two adults book at least 30 days ahead their share falls from 70 to 60 and the family total becomes 90 euros. A couple booking a month out pays 60 rather than 70.

Still unclear: the page does not say whether the 30 euro advance price also applies to the 15 euro reduced ticket.

Sources: https://www.visitmuve.it/en/tickets/

posts.title: Schönbrunn Palace tickets 2026: 42 euros for the Palace Ticket
posts.summary: The Palace Ticket is 42 euros for adults and 30 for children aged 6 to 18 in 2026, with fixed admission times and official sales online only.
posts.body:
The Palace Ticket at Schönbrunn costs 42 euros for an adult in 2026, according to the palace's own tickets and prices page, with children aged 6 to 18 at 30 euros. That covers the full route through the palace rooms.

Three tiers, three prices

The State Apartments ticket, the shorter route, is listed at 30 euros for adults and 20 euros for children. The Palace Ticket is 42 and 30. The Classic Pass, which bundles five attractions including the gardens, is 49 euros for adults and 36 for children. The gap between the shortest option and the widest one is 19 euros a head.

Fixed entry times and fake tickets

The palace states that admission is provided with fixed admission times and advises securing a time slot in advance by buying online. It also warns that genuine tickets are sold online exclusively at imperialtickets.com, a direct answer to resale sites charging a markup. The palace runs daily 8.30am to 5.30pm and last admission to individual attractions is 45 minutes before closing.

Worked example

Two adults and two children on the Palace Ticket pay 42 plus 42 plus 30 plus 30, which is 144 euros. The same family on the Classic Pass pays 49 plus 49 plus 36 plus 36, or 170 euros, so the upgrade costs 26 euros. A couple on the Palace Ticket pays 84 euros.

Still unclear: the page does not state a free age for infants, so families with a child under 6 should confirm before booking.

Sources: https://www.schoenbrunn.at/en/tickets-and-prices/all-tickets-tours

posts.title: Warsaw Rising Museum tickets 2026: 35 zloty
posts.summary: A single ticket is 35 zloty and a discount ticket 30 zloty in 2026, and the museum is closed every Tuesday, which is the expensive part.
posts.body:
A single ticket to the Warsaw Rising Museum costs 35 zloty in 2026, according to the museum's own English visitor pages, with a discount ticket at 30 zloty per person. It remains one of the cheaper major museums in any European capital.

The price and the discount

The museum publishes two figures and no more: single ticket 35 PLN and discount ticket 30 PLN per person. The conditions attached to the discount are not spelled out there, which matters if you are travelling with students or seniors and want a firm budget. Tickets are sold through the museum's own booking site as well as at the desk.

The closed day that catches people

The museum opens Monday and Wednesday to Friday from 08:00 to 18:00, and Saturday and Sunday from 10:00 to 18:00. It is closed on Tuesday. A Tuesday plan is the costly mistake here, because the museum sits well away from the Old Town and the journey is wasted.

Worked example

A couple pays 70 zloty. Two adults and two children pay 35 plus 35 plus 30 plus 30, which is 130 zloty, assuming the children qualify for the reduced rate. No family ticket is published, so there is no bundle to chase.

Still unclear: who exactly qualifies for the 30 zloty discount ticket, and whether the museum still runs a free entry day.

Sources: https://www.1944.pl/en

posts.title: Zoo Zurich tickets 2026: 32 francs for an adult
posts.summary: Adult entry is CHF 32 in 2026, children 6 to 12 pay CHF 18, and the student and senior discount is available only at the box office.
posts.body:
Adult admission to Zoo Zurich costs 32 Swiss francs in 2026, according to the zoo's own tickets page, and the online price is valid only for the date you choose. It is the most visited paid attraction in the city.

What each age pays

The zoo lists adults aged 18 and over at CHF 32, young people aged 13 to 17 at CHF 27 and children aged 6 to 12 at CHF 18. Children under 6 enter free. A family day pass covering two adults with their own children aged 6 to 17 is CHF 85.

The discount you cannot get online

Students and visitors aged 64 and over receive 10 percent off single admission from Monday to Friday with valid identification, but the zoo states this applies at the box office only. Buying online at home therefore costs an older couple more than queueing at the gate on a weekday. Children up to 12 also enter free on their birthday on presentation of valid identification.

Worked example

Two adults and two children aged 6 to 12 pay 32 plus 32 plus 18 plus 18, which is 100 francs, so the 85 franc family day pass saves 15. A couple aged over 64 buying at the counter on a Tuesday pays about 57.60 rather than 64.

Still unclear: the tickets page does not publish daily opening hours, so arrival times have to be taken from the separate visit pages.

Sources: https://www.zoo.ch/en/plan-your-visit/tickets

posts.title: Rijksmuseum tickets 2026: 25 euros, free for under 19s
posts.summary: Adult admission is 25 euros in 2026 and everyone aged 18 and under is free, but booking a start time is required for every visitor.
posts.body:
Admission to the Rijksmuseum costs 25 euros for an adult in 2026, according to the museum's own visit page, and anyone aged 18 and under gets in free. That free age band is unusually generous for a major European museum.

The booking rule that costs people the day

The museum states that booking a start time is required for a visit, and that this applies to everyone, including Museumkaart holders. Turning up with a valid pass and no time slot is not enough. On busy days the early slots go first, so the real cost of skipping the booking step is either a long wait or a change of plan.

Opening days

The Rijksmuseum is open every day between 9am and 5pm, including all public holidays. There is no weekly closing day, which removes the usual Monday trap that catches visitors elsewhere in Europe.

Worked example

A couple pays 50 euros. Two adults with two teenagers aged 18 and 15 also pay 50 euros, because both children are free. A family with three children under 19 still pays only the two adult tickets, which makes the museum one of the cheapest large attractions in Amsterdam for families.

Still unclear: the visit page quotes a single 25 euro figure and does not show whether temporary exhibitions carry a supplement.

Sources: https://www.rijksmuseum.nl/en/visit

posts.title: Casa Batlló tickets 2026: from 29 euros, under 13s free
posts.summary: A general visit starts at 29 euros in 2026 and children aged 0 to 12 are free, with the site advertising savings of up to 15 euros per person for booking ahead.
posts.body:
